items.title: IP final value
items.description: The response reports the ionization potential IP of X as 11.835 eV (accepting 11.84 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question a; reference gives a = 11.835 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving IP = 1.18 eV or 15.19 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; final requested quantity, correctness depends on it.

validation.gold_why: Reports a = IP = 11.835 eV.

items.title: EA final value
items.description: The response reports the electron affinity EA of X as 3.358 eV (accepting 3.36 eV).

provenance.evidence_detail: Required deliverable for sub-question b; reference gives b = 3.358 eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response giving EA = 0.336 eV or 6.71 eV or any other wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; final requested quantity, correctness depends on it.

validation.gold_why: Reports b = EA = 3.358 eV.

items.title: Step 1 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 1 energy balance for the transfer of one electron between the two halves of atoms as (N/2)×(IP − EA) = 409 kJ, with EA subtracted because electron attachment releases energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and correct rollouts use IP − EA for step 1; pitfall EA-sign-in-step-1 addresses the wrong move of adding EA.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 409 kJ or signs EA incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but load-bearing equation; absorbed avoidance of EA-as-positive-cost.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a−b) = 409 kJ step; EA subtracted.

items.title: Step 2 energy balance
items.description: The response writes the step 2 energy balance for converting X⁻ ions to X⁺ as (N/2)×(IP + EA) = 733 kJ, because removing the extra electron costs +EA and ionizing the neutral costs +IP.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses a + b for step 2; pitfall Step-2-electron-count and EA-sign-in-step-2 address the wrong moves.
provenance.discriminates: A response that models X⁻ → X⁺ as one-electron removal costing only IP, giving (N/2)×IP = 733 kJ.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; combined with avoidance of EA-as-release-in-step-2 pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Writes (N/2)(a+b) = 733 kJ step; EA added.

items.title: Two-electron removal
items.description: The response states that converting each X⁻ ion to X⁺ requires removing two electrons: one reversing the electron affinity (costing +EA) and one the ionization of X (costing +IP).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Step 2 electron count', severity high.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats X⁻ → X⁺ as a single-electron transition costing only IP.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key physical reasoning, absorbed one-electron-model pitfall.

validation.gold_why: States X⁻ loses two electrons: +EA then +IP.

items.title: Uses N/2 not N
items.description: The response uses N/2 = 3.0115×10²³ as the number of electron-transfer pairs in each energy-balance equation, not the full Avogadro's number N = 6.023×10²³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Using N instead of N/2', severity medium; reference uses N/2 throughout.
provenance.discriminates: A response that plugs full N into both equations, halving all per-atom eV values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but essential for correct scaling; absorbed using-full-N pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Uses N/2 in both energy-balance equations.

items.title: kJ to J conversion
items.description: The response converts the given energies to joules as 409×10³ J and 733×10³ J before dividing by N/2 and converting to eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'kJ to J omitted', severity medium.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 409 and 733 directly in J, making final values too small by 1000×.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but necessary unit step; absorbed dropping-kJ-to-J pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Uses 409×10³ and 733×10³ (J conversion).

items.title: eV conversion factor
items.description: The response uses the conversion 1 eV = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J to convert per-atom joule energies into eV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to obtain eV.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits this conversion or uses an incorrect factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives but necessary for obtaining correct eV values.

validation.gold_why: Divides by 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ to convert to eV.

items.title: IP minus EA intermediate
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP − EA = 8.477 eV from the 409 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a − b = 8.477; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 0.8476 due to an exponent error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP − EA = 0.8476 eV or any value other than ~8.48 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; load-bearing intermediate result for solving the system.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a−b = 8.477 eV.

items.title: IP plus EA intermediate
items.description: The response obtains the intermediate value IP + EA = 15.194 eV from the 733 kJ step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a + b = 15.194; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 1.5194.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP + EA = 1.5194 eV or any value other than ~15.19 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; critical intermediate, both flawed responses missed it.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a+b = 15.194 eV.

items.title: Avoids exponent slip
items.description: Avoids writing the per-atom energy for the 409 kJ step as ~1.358×10⁻¹⁹ J; the correct per-atom value obtained by dividing 409×10³ by N/2 is ~1.358×10⁻¹⁸ J.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exponent in J/eV conversion', severity medium, observed in rollout 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response containing the off-by-10 exponent error that propagates to all final values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; observed arithmetic error in exponent of per-atom energy.

validation.gold_why: No per-atom value written incorrectly; correct method used.

items.title: Both quantities reported
items.description: The response reports both IP and EA values in eV for the atoms of X, explicitly labelled, rather than stopping after solving only one of the two.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Only one quantity reported', severity low; answer format demands two labelled values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only IP or only EA.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 0/2 negatives; adds completeness check beyond individual values.

validation.gold_why: Reports both a (IP) and b (EA) in eV.

items.title: Simultaneous equations solved
items.description: The response solves the two simultaneous equations (IP − EA = 8.477 and IP + EA = 15.194) to obtain IP and EA, e.g. by adding and subtracting the two equations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly solves the system to reach a = 11.835 and b = 3.358.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to combine the two balances into solved IP and EA values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; both flawed responses failed to solve the system.

validation.gold_why: Solves simultaneous equations for a and b.

items.title: Full expression for IP−EA
items.description: The response writes the full substituted expression (409×10³×2)/(1.602×10⁻¹⁹×6.023×10²³) for IP − EA, showing all constants.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a − b = 8.477; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 0.8476 due to an exponent error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP − EA = 0.8476 eV or any value other than ~8.48 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Extends item 9 to verify computational setup; grounds the 8.477 result.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a−b = 8.477 eV.

items.title: Full expression for IP+EA
items.description: The response writes the full substituted expression (733×10³×2)/(1.602×10⁻¹⁹×6.023×10²³) for IP + EA, showing all constants.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference gives a + b = 15.194; rollout 3 wrongly obtained 1.5194.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IP + EA = 1.5194 eV or any value other than ~15.19 eV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Extends item 10 to verify computational setup; grounds the 15.194 result.

validation.gold_why: Obtains a+b = 15.194 eV.

items.title: General speed formula
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic relation v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} connecting the wave speed to the bulk modulus and volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on this starting formula; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to final answers without relating them to K and ρ, making the derivation uncheckable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational formula; 0/2 discrimination but necessary intermediate for all speed results.

validation.gold_why: Uses v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} as general acoustic relation.

items.title: General impedance formula
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic impedance relation Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} or equivalently Z = ρv, connecting impedance to bulk modulus and density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} = ρv; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both impedance results.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an inverted impedance formula such as Z = v/ρ or Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational formula; 0/2 discrimination but necessary intermediate for all impedance results.

validation.gold_why: Uses Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} as general impedance relation.

items.title: Isothermal bulk modulus derivation
items.description: The response uses the ideal-gas equation of state P = NT/V under isothermal conditions to derive the isothermal bulk modulus K = P.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) requires the isothermal bulk modulus as an intermediate to derive v_T and Z_T.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses K = γP for the isothermal case, swapping the two limits.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate; 0.50 discrimination, load-bearing for isothermal speed and impedance.

validation.gold_why: States K = P for isothermal process explicitly.

items.title: Adiabatic bulk modulus derivation
items.description: The response uses the adiabatic relation P ∝ V^{−γ} (i.e., PV^γ = const) to derive the adiabatic bulk modulus K = γP.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) requires the adiabatic bulk modulus as an intermediate to derive v_S and Z_S.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses K = P (no γ factor) for the adiabatic case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate; 0.50 discrimination, load-bearing for adiabatic speed and impedance.

validation.gold_why: States K = γP for adiabatic process explicitly.

items.title: Isothermal wave speed
items.description: The response gives the isothermal acoustic wave speed as v = (P/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (T/m)^{1/2}, where ρ is the volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) explicitly asks for the wave speed in the isothermal limit; the reference gives v_T = (P/ρ)^{1/2} = (T/m)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the isothermal speed or gives a wrong expression such as (γP/ρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives v = (P/ρ)^{1/2} = (T/m)^{1/2} for isothermal.

items.title: Isothermal wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the isothermal wave impedance as Z = (Pρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (mT)^{1/2}n where n is the particle density.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) explicitly asks for the wave impedance in the isothermal limit; all consensus attempts and the reference agree on Z_T = (Pρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes only the wave speed and never evaluates the impedance, or gives an inverted formula such as Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives Z = (Pρ)^{1/2} = (mT)^{1/2}n for isothermal.

items.title: Adiabatic wave speed
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic acoustic wave speed as v = (γP/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γT/m)^{1/2}, where γ = C_P/C_V.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) explicitly asks for the wave speed in the adiabatic limit; the reference gives v_S = (γP/ρ)^{1/2} = (γT/m)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that drops the γ factor, writing v_S = (P/ρ)^{1/2} and making it identical to the isothermal case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives v = (γP/ρ)^{1/2} = (γT/m)^{1/2} for adiabatic.

items.title: Adiabatic wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic wave impedance as Z = (γPρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γmT)^{1/2}n.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) explicitly asks for the wave impedance in the adiabatic limit; all consensus attempts and the reference agree on Z_S = (γPρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the adiabatic impedance entirely or drops the γ factor from it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity; 0.50 discrimination, essential to the answer.

validation.gold_why: Gives Z = (γPρ)^{1/2} = (γmT)^{1/2}n for adiabatic.

items.title: Adiabatic exceeds isothermal
items.description: The response states that the adiabatic wave velocity and impedance are larger than the isothermal values by a factor of γ^{1/2}, because γ > 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among attempts and reference that v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = sqrt(γ) > 1; the reference explicitly says adiabatic values are always larger.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two limits give equal results or that isothermal values are larger.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; central comparative result linking both limits.

validation.gold_why: States adiabatic v and Z are larger than isothermal by γ>1.

items.title: Adiabatic index definition
items.description: The response defines γ = C_P/C_V and states that γ > 1 for the ideal classical gas with temperature-independent specific heat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts correctly identified γ = C_P/C_V > 1, and this is load-bearing for the adiabatic results and the comparison between limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses γ ≤ 1 or never defines γ, making the comparison between limits unjustified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but necessary for correctness; defines the key parameter γ.

validation.gold_why: Defines γ = C_P/C_V and states γ > 1.

items.title: High frequency is adiabatic
items.description: The response identifies the adiabatic limit as the one achieved at higher wave frequencies, explaining that the oscillation period is too short for heat exchange.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (iii) asks which limit is achieved at higher frequencies; the reference states the adiabatic result is realistic at usual sound frequencies.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns the isothermal limit to high frequencies, inverting the thermal-relaxation argument.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the frequency sub-question; 0.50 discrimination, essential.

validation.gold_why: Identifies adiabatic as high-frequency limit; too fast for heat exchange.

items.title: Low frequency is isothermal
items.description: The response states that the isothermal process is the low-frequency limit, where the wave's period is long enough for temperature to equilibrate.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference specifies the isothermal case is implemented only at extremely low frequencies where the period allows temperature equilibration over the system size.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly names the high-frequency limit but never explains why the other limit is low-frequency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Complements the high-frequency answer; 0.50 discrimination, important reasoning.

validation.gold_why: States isothermal is low-frequency limit with temperature equilibration.

items.title: Isothermal speed independent of compression
items.description: The response notes that the isothermal wave speed v = (T/m)^{1/2} does not depend on the static compression or ambient pressure of the gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states 'v does not depend on the static compression of the gas,' a physical observation no attempt made.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats v_T as depending on ambient pressure or density changes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reference-only depth; 0.50 discrimination, adds physical insight without being required.

validation.gold_why: Notes isothermal v does not depend on static compression.

items.title: Avoid frequency-regime reversal
items.description: Avoids claiming that the isothermal limit is achieved at higher wave frequencies or that the adiabatic limit is a low-frequency phenomenon.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Frequency–regime reversal' (severity high): inverting which limit corresponds to high vs low frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the frequency assignments, saying fast oscillations allow temperature equilibration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific reversal trap; 0.50 discrimination, directly mirrors the frequency sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Correctly assigns adiabatic to high frequency, isothermal to low.

items.title: Avoid swapped or omitted gamma
items.description: Avoids using K = P for the adiabatic case, using K = γP for the isothermal case, or writing the adiabatic speed or impedance without the γ factor.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapped bulk modulus' (severity high): mixing up which thermodynamic variable is held constant in ∂P/∂V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interchanges the two limits' bulk moduli, yielding v_T = v_S and Z_T = Z_S with wrong assignments.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Most common mistake family; 0.50 discrimination each, covers swapped modulus and omitted gamma.

validation.gold_why: Uses correct bulk modulus for each case, no swap.

items.title: Immune suppression & infections
items.description: States that sirolimus suppresses the immune system to prevent transplant rejection, leading to an increased risk of infections.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Central well-known side effect; 0/3 discrimination but essential content.

items.description: States that sirolimus is associated with delayed wound healing attributed to the systemic effects of immune suppression on normal repair processes.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollups and the reference confirm impaired wound healing as a side effect, especially relevant post-transplant.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Recognized side effect; 0/3 discrimination but clinically relevant to transplant patients.

items.title: Oral ulcers identified

provenance.calibration_rationale: Common side effect; 0/3 discrimination but specific and checkable.

items.title: ADPKD progression mention
items.description: States that sirolimus may possibly slow the progression of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, requiring clinicians to carefully balance benefits with management of side effects.

items.title: Opportunistic infections

items.title: Avoids nephrotoxicity conflation

items.description: The response states that space in the operative field is created through one-lung ventilation, allowing the operated lung to deflate or collapse.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Unbounded vs. infinite' (high severity) and 'Stopping at arbitrarily large' (medium severity): treating unboundedness as equivalent to the existence of s = ∞.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes 'spin can become infinite' because J_max = Ns diverges as N increases, without distinguishing the two claims.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; addresses a key conceptual confusion in the question.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: Singular thermodynamic limit
items.description: States that taking the number of particles to infinite is a singular or thermodynamic limit rather than a spin eigenvalue in a finite-dimensional representation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Thermodynamic limit as ordinary' (medium severity): describing the N→∞ limit as yielding a well-defined quantum state with S = ∞.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the N→∞ limit as producing a standard spin-s state with s = ∞ satisfying the usual angular momentum algebra.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1.00 discrimination; resolves the N→∞ case with precise mathematical framing.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: J_max = Ns formula
items.description: States that for N identical spin-s particles the maximum total spin quantum number is J_max = Ns.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on notation: one used N/2 (spin-1/2 only), two used Ns (general). The general formula Ns is correct; N/2 is the special case s = 1/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes J_max = N/2 as the general maximum total spin for N identical particles of arbitrary spin s.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.00 discrimination but provides concrete quantitative anchor for composite spin.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: Spin-1/2 max N/2
items.description: States that for N spin-1/2 particles specifically, the maximum total spin quantum number is N/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 1 used N/2 for spin-1/2; rollouts 2 and 3 used Ns generally. Both are internally correct; N/2 is the spin-1/2 special case worth noting explicitly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the general formula Ns without recognizing the common spin-1/2 case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1.00 discrimination; concrete special case that caught every flawed response.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: Continuous-spin ≠ s=∞
items.description: Distinguishes Wigner continuous-spin representations of the Poincaré group from a spin quantum number s = ∞, noting they are labeled by a continuous parameter rather than being infinite spin.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Continuous-spin ≠ infinite spin' (high severity): conflating continuous-spin representations with particles whose spin quantum number is literally infinity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats continuous-spin representations as proof that elementary particles can have s = ∞.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; prevents a common conflation in the theoretical context.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: Continuous-spin unobserved
items.description: Notes that continuous-spin representations of the Poincaré group have infinitely many polarization states and remain unobserved in nature.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three attempts mentioned that continuous-spin representations are unobserved/pathological; this is a consensus claim adding physical context.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions continuous-spin representations without noting their absence from observed physics.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.00 discrimination but adds real physical context to the theoretical discussion.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: Helicity for massless
items.description: States that massless particles are classified by helicity rather than an ordinary spin quantum number in the same sense as massive particles.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Helicity vs. spin for massless' (medium severity): treating massless particles as having ordinary spin s rather than helicity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the photon has 'spin 1' identically to massive spin-1 particles and then asks whether that spin could be infinite.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; relevant distinction for massless particle spin.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: ISO(2) little group
items.description: Mentions ISO(2) as the little group for massless particles in the Poincaré group context.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three attempts identified the little group structure; ISO(2) for massless particles is a consensus technical detail.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses helicity for massless particles without naming the underlying little group.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.50 discrimination; provides technical detail for the massless-particle case.

validation.gold_why: Not mentioned in reference answer.

items.title: Avoids classical spin
items.description: Avoids invoking classical angular momentum as a substitute for quantum mechanical spin without explicitly noting the concept distinction between the two.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: 'Do not invoke classical angular momentum as a substitute for quantum mechanical spin unless explicitly noting the distinction.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers using classical L = r × p arguments without addressing quantum mechanical spin quantization.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.00 discrimination; low-weight guard against a common conceptual error.

validation.gold_why: No classical angular momentum invoked.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Destructive interference condition
items.description: Uses the destructive interference condition 2n₁t = λ/2 with n₁ = 1.2 and λ = 5000 Å for the coating film in part (a).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes 2n₁t = λ/2 as the condition for antiphase reflected beams.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 2n₁t = mλ (one net π shift) or 2n₁t = λ (wrong condition).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core formula for part (a); caught 1/2 negatives, essential for deriving thickness.

validation.gold_why: Uses 2n₁t = λ/2 explicitly.

items.title: Minimum thickness value
items.description: States the minimum coating thickness as t = λ/(4n₁) = 0.10 μm (or approximately 1042 Å) for part (a).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) asks for the minimum thickness; the reference gives t = λ/(4n₁) = 0.10 μm.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes 2083 Å or 868 Å instead of 1042 Å.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct answer to part (a); caught 1/2 negatives, correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: States t = λ/(4n₁) = 0.10 μm.

items.title: Both reflections phase-shifted
items.description: States that both reflected beams undergo a π phase shift because each reflection occurs at a boundary to higher refractive index (air→1.2 and 1.2→1.4).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference and implicit constraints note both interfaces produce π shifts because n increases at each boundary.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims only one reflected beam acquires a π phase shift.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; gold=FAIL but physically necessary to justify the λ/2 condition.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly state both beams undergo π phase shift.

items.title: Net reflection phase difference zero
items.description: States that the net reflection-induced phase difference between the two reflected beams is zero because both acquire the same π shift at the coating surfaces.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference's condition 2n₁t = λ/2 (not 2n₁t = mλ) implicitly requires zero net reflection phase difference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims a net π phase difference from the two reflections, leading to the wrong interference condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; load-bearing intermediate explaining why 2n₁t = λ/2 suffices.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly state net reflection phase difference is zero.

items.title: Unequal coefficients explanation
items.description: Part (b) explains that the reflected intensity is small but not zero because the reflection coefficients at the two surfaces of the coating are unequal (R₁ ≠ R₂).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks why reflection is small but not zero; the reference shows R₁ ≠ R₂.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims destructive interference alone should give zero, or that does not identify unequal amplitudes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the 'explain' part of (b); caught 1/2 negatives, central to correctness.

validation.gold_why: Explains R₁ ≠ R₂ causes nonzero reflected intensity.

items.title: Antiphase with unequal amplitudes
items.description: States that the two reflected beams are in antiphase (destructive interference) but have unequal amplitudes, so cancellation is incomplete.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference shows the beams interfere destructively (antiphase) but R₁ ≠ R₂ prevents full cancellation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the beams are not in antiphase, or that equal amplitudes are not required for cancellation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; provides the physical mechanism behind the nonzero resultant intensity.

validation.gold_why: States destructive interference but unequal intensities, incomplete cancellation.

items.title: Reflection coefficient formula
items.description: Gives a reflection coefficient formula — R = [(n_A − n_B)/(n_A + n_B)]² or r = (n_A − n_B)/(n_A + n_B) — for the surfaces of the coating.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses R = [(nA − nB)/(nA + nB)]²; rollouts used the amplitude version r, both physically valid.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains unequal reflection qualitatively without providing the quantitative formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination (0/2); useful intermediate but not directly tested by flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: Gives R = [(nA−nB)/(nA+nB)]² formula.

items.title: Specific coefficient values
items.description: Computes the reflection coefficient at the air–coating interface as R₁ = ((1.2 − 1.0)/(1.2 + 1.0))² and at the coating–glass interface as R₂ = ((1.2 − 1.4)/(1.2 + 1.4))².

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly computes R₁ and R₂ using n₀ = 1, n₁ = 1.2, n₂ = 1.4.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the coefficients are equal without computing them, or that computes them incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; concrete values demonstrate why R₁ ≠ R₂ for the given indices.

validation.gold_why: Writes R₁ and R₂ with correct symbolic index values.

items.title: Zero-reflection amplitude condition
items.description: States that zero reflected intensity requires the reflection coefficients at the two surfaces of the coating to be equal, R₁ = R₂.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference sets R₁ = R₂ as the condition for zero resultant reflected light.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims thickness alone can produce zero reflection without addressing amplitude matching.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key reasoning step linking equal reflection amplitudes to perfect cancellation.

validation.gold_why: States R₁ = R₂ required for zero reflection.

items.title: Ideal coating index value
items.description: States the ideal coating index for zero reflection as n′ = √(n₀n₂) = √(1 × 1.4) ≈ 1.18.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) requires the changed index value; the reference gives n' = √(n₀n₂) = 1.18.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 1.2 (arithmetic mean), 1.3, or no ideal index.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct answer to part (b); caught 1/2 negatives, correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: States n' = √(n₀n₂) = 1.18.

items.title: Geometric mean derivation
items.description: Derives n′ = √(n₀n₂) from the condition R₁ = R₂ for the two surfaces of the coating.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference solves (n'−n₀)/(n'+n₀) = (n'−n₂)/(n'+n₂) to obtain n' = √(n₀n₂).
provenance.discriminates: A response that states n' = 1.18 without deriving it, or that derives it from the wrong condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; required intermediate showing how the ideal index follows from equal coefficients.

validation.gold_why: Derives n' = √(n₀n₂) from R₁ = R₂ condition.

items.title: Change index not thickness
items.description: States that the coating refractive index must be changed (rather than the thickness) to make the reflected intensity zero.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks 'what needs to be changed'; the reference changes n₁ to n', not t.
provenance.discriminates: A response that suggests adjusting the thickness further or changing the wavelength to achieve zero reflection.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; answers what needs changing in part (b), distinguishes index from thickness.

validation.gold_why: States index must change, not thickness.

items.title: Magnitude of index change
items.description: States that the coating index of 1.2 must decrease by approximately 0.02 to reach the ideal value of about 1.18.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks 'by how much'; reference and consensus give Δn ≈ −0.017.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the target value 1.18 without the magnitude of the change, or gives the wrong direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; gold=FAIL but question explicitly asks 'by how much,' so required for completeness.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly state decrease of 0.017 from 1.2.

items.title: Avoids one-phase-shift thickness
items.description: Avoids stating the minimum thickness as 5000/(2 × 1.2) ≈ 2083 Å, which would result from counting only one π phase shift at the coating surfaces.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'One phase shift counted' and 'Admits only one phase shift' pitfalls both produce d ≈ 2083 Å.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 2083 Å as the minimum coating thickness.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific trap observed where the wrong condition 2n₁t = λ is used.

validation.gold_why: Gives 0.10 μm, not 2083 Å.

items.title: Avoids arithmetic mean index
items.description: Avoids claiming the ideal coating index equals the arithmetic mean (1 + 1.4)/2 = 1.2, which would imply no change is needed since the given coating already has n₁ = 1.2.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Arithmetic mean for index' pitfall yields exactly 1.2, creating false confirmation that the given index is already ideal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes the given n₁ = 1.2 already satisfies the zero-reflection condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination (0/2) but a genuine conceptual trap: arithmetic mean coincidentally equals 1.2.

validation.gold_why: States ideal index 1.18, not arithmetic mean 1.2.

items.title: 157.836 peak composition
items.description: Assigns the 157.836 peak to the Br2 molecule composed of two atoms of the lighter bromine isotope.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires isotopic composition of each peak; consensus among all correct rollouts assigns 157.836 to ^79Br2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns 157.836 to the mixed heavy-light composition or to the heavy-heavy composition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core peak assignment; 0/2 caught but essential for all downstream results.

validation.gold_why: Reference gives no peak assignments at all.

items.title: 159.834 peak composition
items.description: Assigns the 159.834 peak to the Br2 molecule composed of one atom of each bromine isotope.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires isotopic composition of each peak; consensus assigns 159.834 to ^79Br^81Br.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns 159.834 to a homonuclear isotopologue or fails to identify it as the mixed species.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core peak assignment; 0/2 caught but essential for isotope mass derivation.

validation.gold_why: Reference gives no peak assignments at all.

items.title: 161.832 peak composition
items.description: Assigns the 161.832 peak to the Br2 molecule composed of two atoms of the heavier bromine isotope.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires isotopic composition of each peak; consensus assigns 161.832 to ^81Br2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns 161.832 to the light-light or light-heavy composition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core peak assignment; 0/2 caught but essential for all downstream results.

validation.gold_why: Reference gives no peak assignments at all.

items.title: Light isotope mass
items.description: Reports the mass of the lighter bromine isotope as 78.918 u, derived by halving the 157.836 peak rather than the 159.834 peak.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Halving the mixed peak': dividing 159.834 by 2 gives 79.917 u, a spurious single isotope mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 79.917 u as an isotope mass or derives both isotope masses from the 159.834 peak.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbs avoidance of halving mixed peak; 0/2 caught but load-bearing value.

validation.gold_why: Reference halves no peaks at all.

items.title: Heavy isotope mass
items.description: Reports the mass of the heavier bromine isotope as 80.916 u, derived by halving the 161.832 peak rather than the 159.834 peak.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Halving the mixed peak': dividing 159.834 by 2 gives 79.917 u, a spurious single isotope mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 79.917 u as an isotope mass or derives both isotope masses from the 159.834 peak.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbs avoidance of halving mixed peak; 0/2 caught but load-bearing value.

validation.gold_why: Reference halves no peaks at all.

items.title: Middle peak consistency
items.description: Verifies that the two individual isotope masses sum to 159.834 u, matching the given middle peak (78.918 + 80.916 = 159.834).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus check: all correct rollouts verified that the sum of the two isotope masses reproduces the 159.834 middle peak.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports isotope masses that do not sum to 159.834, indicating an arithmetic or assignment error.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Useful cross-check; 0/2 caught, moderate importance to correctness.

validation.gold_why: Reference performs no consistency check.

items.title: Average Br2 mass
items.description: Reports the average mass of a Br2 molecule as approximately 159.8 u, computed as a weighted sum of the three peaks using their relative sizes (accepting 159.790–159.806 u).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverged on whether to normalize by the 0.9999 sum of relative sizes; both 159.790 u and 159.806 u are defensible.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 159.834 u (simple mean) or a value outside 159.790–159.806 u, indicating use of an unweighted average or another error.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; directly requested quantity with proven discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no average Br2 mass.

items.title: Average atomic mass
items.description: Reports the average atomic mass of a bromine atom as approximately 79.9 u, obtained by dividing the average Br2 mass by two rather than reporting the molecular mass directly (accepting 79.895–79.903 u).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts derived this from their respective Br2 averages; values diverged between 79.895 u and 79.903 u depending on normalization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports ~159.8 u as the atomic mass (forgetting to halve) or a value outside 79.895–79.903 u.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbs molecular-vs-atomic avoidance; caught 1/2 negatives, directly requested.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no average atomic mass.

items.title: Light isotope square root
items.description: Derives the fractional abundance of the lighter bromine isotope by taking the square root of 0.2569, yielding 0.5069.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among correct rollouts: p = sqrt(0.2569) = 0.5069, because the 157.836 peak intensity equals p squared.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 0.2569 directly as the abundance without the square-root step.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key derivation step enabling abundance calculation.

validation.gold_why: Reference shows no square-root derivation.

items.title: Heavy isotope square root
items.description: Derives the fractional abundance of the heavier bromine isotope by taking the square root of 0.2431, yielding 0.4931.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among correct rollouts: q = sqrt(0.2431) = 0.4931, because the 161.832 peak intensity equals q squared.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 0.2431 directly as the abundance without the square-root step.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; key derivation step enabling abundance calculation.

validation.gold_why: Reference shows no square-root derivation.

items.title: Light isotope abundance
items.description: Reports the percent abundance of the lighter bromine isotope as 50.69% (accepting 50.6–50.7%).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) requires percent abundance of the two isotopes; consensus value is 50.69%.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 25.69% (using the raw 0.2569 peak size) or any other incorrect abundance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; final requested quantity with high importance.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no percent abundances.

items.title: Heavy isotope abundance
items.description: Reports the percent abundance of the heavier bromine isotope as 49.31% (accepting 49.2–49.4%).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) requires percent abundance of the two isotopes; consensus value is 49.31%.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 24.31% (using the raw 0.2431 peak size) or any other incorrect abundance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; final requested quantity with high importance.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no percent abundances.

items.title: 2pq verification
items.description: Verifies that 2pq equals the 0.4999 middle peak relative size, using p = 0.5069 and q = 0.4931, treating the middle peak as 2pq rather than pq.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Middle peak as pq not 2pq': using 0.4999 = pq alongside p² = 0.2569 yields inconsistent or impossible abundances.
provenance.discriminates: A response that sets up equations using pq = 0.4999 instead of 2pq = 0.4999, leading to inconsistent abundances.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbs pq-vs-2pq avoidance; caught 1/2 negatives, but verification only.

validation.gold_why: Reference derives no abundances from peaks.

items.title: Isotope mass spacing
items.description: Reports or uses the mass difference between the two bromine isotopes as 1.998 u, consistent with the peak spacing between 157.836 and 159.834.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus value: isotope mass difference is 1.998 u, matching the spacing between adjacent Br2 peaks.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports an incorrect spacing or fails to recognize the 1.998 u gap between isotope masses.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 caught; minor derived quantity, real but low added depth.

validation.gold_why: Reference reports no mass spacing.

items.title: Avoids raw peak as abundance
items.description: Avoids reporting the 0.2569 or 0.2431 relative sizes directly as the percent abundance of either bromine isotope, instead applying the square-root relationship.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Peak abundance as atomic abundance': taking 0.2569 directly as atomic abundance gives 25.69% instead of 50.69%.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 25.69% and 24.31% as the two isotope abundances, skipping the square-root step.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific observed trap of conflating peak size with abundance.

validation.gold_why: Reference applies no square-root relationship.

provenance.discriminates: A response that answers TNF-α or names infliximab/adalimumab as the subsequent drug.

items.title: Saddle-point condition
items.description: The saddle-point condition is stated as (p ± A(t_s))²/2 + I_p = 0, requiring the kinetic energy to equal −I_p and thereby forcing the complex saddle-point time t_s to be complex.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing I_p in saddle condition' (high severity): writing (p+A)²/2 = 0 instead of (p+A)²/2 + I_p = 0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits I_p from the saddle-point equation, leaving t_s real and losing all tunneling attenuation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core derivation step; caught 1/2 negatives. Forces complex time, load-bearing for the question.

validation.gold_why: Saddle-point condition with I_p not stated.

items.title: Complex time contour
items.description: The ionization amplitude is evaluated along a complex time contour that passes through the complex saddle-point time t_s in the lower or upper half-plane.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus that t_s must be complex and the action is evaluated along a complex time contour.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only integrates along the real time axis with no complex-time deformation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives. Establishes the imaginary-time integration path central to the derivation.

validation.gold_why: Complex contour evaluation not described.

items.title: Static WKB exponent
items.description: In the static or quasistatic limit the ionization amplitude exponent is given as exp[−(2 I_p)^{3/2} / (3|E|)], with the factor 2^{3/2} present.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus static WKB amplitude exponent is M ~ exp[-(2 I_p)^{3/2} / (3|E|)].
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes I_p^{3/2}/(3|E|) or omits the factor 2^{3/2} from kinetic energy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Canonical result; missing the 2^{3/2} factor is a common serious error.

validation.gold_why: Static WKB exponent not given.

items.title: Rate exponent doubled
items.description: The ionization rate W ~ |M|² carries the exponent exp[−2(2 I_p)^{3/2} / (3|E|)], differing by a factor of 2 from the amplitude exponent.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Amplitude vs rate exponent' (medium severity): reporting the amplitude exponent as the rate exponent without squaring.
provenance.discriminates: A response that quotes the same exponent for both the amplitude and the rate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Distinguishing amplitude from rate exponent is a key intermediate distinction.

validation.gold_why: Rate exponent doubling not stated.

items.title: Static imaginary tunneling time
items.description: The static-limit imaginary tunneling time parameter is given as τ_s = √(2 I_p) / |E|, identified as the imaginary-time extent of the under-barrier segment.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus value τ_s = sqrt(2 I_p) / |E| for the static imaginary tunneling time.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a different formula or no expression for the imaginary-time scale.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives. Directly addresses the time-spent-under-barrier sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Static imaginary tunneling time not given.

items.title: Barrier exit coordinate
items.description: The static-limit barrier exit coordinate is given as z_exit = I_p / |E|, locating where the electron emerges in the continuum.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus barrier exit coordinate z_exit = I_p / |E|.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives an incorrect exit coordinate or conflates it with I_p^{3/2}/|E|.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Concrete intermediate result adding physical grounding to the tunneling picture.

validation.gold_why: Barrier exit coordinate not given.

items.title: Real part as exit time
items.description: Re(t_s) is identified as the real time at which the electron exits the tunneling barrier and appears in the continuum, not the moment of release from the atomic core.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Conflating exit time with ionization time' (medium severity): identifying Re(t_s) as release from atom rather than barrier exit.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says Re(t_s) is when the electron is released from the atom or starts tunneling.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Central physical interpretation of the complex saddle-point time.

validation.gold_why: Re(t_s) as exit time not identified.

items.title: Imaginary part as attenuation
items.description: Im(t_s) is identified as an imaginary-time attenuation parameter that controls the exponential suppression of the ionization amplitude during tunneling, not as a real clock time.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus that Im(t_s) is an imaginary-time attenuation parameter along a complex contour.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats Im(t_s) as a literal real-valued duration that can be directly measured.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Essential physical interpretation of the imaginary part; directly asked.

validation.gold_why: Im(t_s) as attenuation parameter not identified.

items.title: Under-barrier time subtleties
items.description: The relation between the imaginary-time interval and a possible real under-barrier traversal time is explicitly discussed, stating that no unique real tunneling time exists and that mapping τ_s to a physical time is model-dependent.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Leaving under-barrier time unanswered' and 'Equating imaginary time to real time' (both medium/high): failing to connect Im(t_s) to traversal time or asserting it is directly measurable.
provenance.discriminates: A response that either drops sub-question (c) entirely or claims τ_s is a directly measurable real tunneling time.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Directly addresses the disputed point about time spent under the barrier.

validation.gold_why: Subtleties of real tunneling time not explicitly discussed.

items.title: Sign-convention consistency
items.description: Avoids mixing the exp(−iS) and exp(+iΦ) conventions without flipping the sign of Im(t_s), so that the ionization amplitude always carries a decaying exponential under the barrier rather than a growing one.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Exponent sign / growth error' (high severity): mixing E convention signs produces a growing exponential.
provenance.discriminates: A response that pairs exp(−iS) with t_s = t_0 − iτ_s (or exp(+iΦ) with t_s = t_0 + iτ_s), giving exponential growth instead of decay.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives. Specific trap; discounted for avoidance-item structural advantage.

validation.gold_why: Sign conventions not addressed at all.

items.title: Keldysh regime and tunneling
items.description: The tunneling treatment is stated to apply in the Keldysh-parameter regime γ ≲ 1, where the strong laser field drives tunneling ionization rather than multiphoton absorption.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint in the question structure specifies Keldysh parameter γ ≲ 1 and that tunneling is the dominant process.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies the formalism in a multiphoton regime γ ≫ 1 without noting the tunneling requirement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Specifies the physical regime for the entire derivation.

validation.gold_why: Keldysh parameter not mentioned.

items.title: Sum over saddle points
items.description: The total ionization amplitude is written as a sum over saddle-point contributions, M ~ Σ_s prefactor_s × exp[−i S(t_s)], reflecting multiple complex emission times in a periodic laser field.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus form M_p ~ sum_s prefactor_s * exp[-i S(p,t_s)].
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only a single saddle-point contribution for a periodic laser field without summation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives. Captures the multi-saddle structure of the ionization amplitude in a laser field.

validation.gold_why: Sum over saddle points not written.

items.title: Imaginary momentum under barrier
items.description: Along the under-barrier portion of the complex time contour the electron's kinetic momentum (p ± A(t)) is stated to be imaginary, which produces the exponential attenuation of the ionization amplitude.

provenance.evidence_detail: Question structure implicit constraint: 'The under-barrier portion corresponds to a segment where the canonical momentum is imaginary or the velocity is imaginary.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the under-barrier momentum as real-valued throughout.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Key mechanism linking imaginary time to exponential suppression.

validation.gold_why: Imaginary momentum under barrier not stated.

items.title: Steepest-descent prefactor
items.description: The Gaussian steepest-descent prefactor of the form √(2π / S″(t_s)) (or equivalent with consistent sign convention) is included in the saddle-point expression for the ionization amplitude.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverged on the exact form of the prefactor due to sign conventions, but all included a Gaussian saddle-point prefactor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives no prefactor or a nonsensical one unrelated to the second derivative of the action at the saddle.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Technical completeness of the saddle-point expression; secondary to interpretation.

validation.gold_why: Steepest-descent prefactor not included.

items.title: Energy conservation at saddle
items.description: Energy conservation is explained to be enforced at the complex saddle-point time rather than strictly along the real time axis, which is the role of the complex saddle-point condition in simplifying the integration.

provenance.evidence_detail: Question structure implicit constraint: 'Energy conservation is enforced at complex saddle points rather than strictly on the real time axis.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims energy is conserved only on the real time axis or does not mention the complex-saddle energy condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives. Explains why the complex time enters the derivation at all.

validation.gold_why: Energy conservation at saddle not explained.

items.title: Candidate real-time definitions
items.description: At least one candidate definition for a real tunneling time (e.g., Larmor, Büttiker–Landauer, or PEWCS) is mentioned, noting that these give model-dependent results when related to the imaginary-time saddle-point parameter.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Equating imaginary time to real time' references Larmor, Büttiker–Landauer etc. as model-dependent mappings.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives no real-time tunneling-time framework and simply asserts or denies a physical time without any named alternative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives. Adds depth to the disputed-point discussion of under-barrier time.

validation.gold_why: No candidate real-time definitions mentioned.

items.title: Avoids HBsAg

provenance.discriminates: A response that does not clarify why the IgM subclass of anti-HBc is the wrong choice for a remote illness.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; targets confusion between total and IgM anti-HBc.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that no signs of increased ICP and acute onset exclude a posterior fossa mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects C based on hyperpigmented macules or without addressing the acute timeline.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL, caught 1/2 negatives. Necessary differential exclusion; modest weight given gold failure.

validation.gold_why: Does not discuss posterior fossa malignancy exclusion.

items.title: Excludes peripheral demyelination
items.description: The response cites the 5/5 strength in the upper and lower extremities and present deep tendon reflexes bilaterally as evidence against peripheral nerve demyelination.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that intact strength and present reflexes exclude peripheral neuropathy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects D despite 5/5 strength and present reflexes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL, caught 1/2 negatives. Strength 5/5 is a key exam finding refuting option D.

validation.gold_why: Does not cite 5/5 strength excluding GBS.

items.title: Pitfall: macules not NF1
items.description: Avoids interpreting the faint hyperpigmented macules on the chest as café-au-lait spots of NF1 to justify posterior fossa malignancy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Macules → NF1 → tumor' warns against misidentifying skin lesions to select option C.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects C by conflating hyperpigmented macules with café-au-lait spots and NF1-associated CNS tumors.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass, caught 1/2 negatives. Specific trap in this question's presentation.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention macules or NF1.

items.title: Pitfall: no rash does not exclude VZV
items.description: Avoids discarding varicella zoster infection as the cause solely because no preceding chickenpox rash is documented in the history.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'No rash → exclude VZV' warns against eliminating B for lack of rash history.
provenance.discriminates: A response that eliminates B because no rash is described, leading to A, C, or D.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass, caught 2/2 negatives. High-discrimination pitfall directly observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: States chickenpox may not have been recognized.

items.title: Subclinical varicella
items.description: The response states that the preceding varicella infection may have been subclinical or unrecognized by the family.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer notes the varicella infection may not have been recognized by the family as chickenpox; no rollout mentioned this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that requires a documented chickenpox rash before considering varicella as the cause.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass, caught 2/2 negatives. Adds depth explaining how VZV fits despite no documented rash.

validation.gold_why: States varicella may not have been recognized by family.

items.title: Energy formula stated
items.description: The response states the energy formula for the one-dimensional Ising model as E = -J Σ_n s_n s_{n+1} (or equivalent notation), where J is the coupling and the sum runs over sites along the chain.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks to derive the energy (Hamiltonian) formula; the reference gives E = -J Σ_n S_n S_{n+1}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a generic Hamiltonian without the specific nearest-neighbor Ising form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core deliverable; caught 1/2 negatives, gold passed, highest importance.

validation.gold_why: E = -J Σ S_n S_{n+1} stated explicitly.

items.title: Negative sign before J
items.description: The energy formula for the Ising model contains a negative sign before the coupling J in the sum over nearest-neighbor spin products, so that E ∝ -J Σ s_i s_{i+1}.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign in Hamiltonian': writing E = +J Σ s_i s_{i+1} inverts ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic behavior.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes E = +J Σ s_i s_{i+1}, making J>0 favor anti-aligned spins.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sign is physics-critical; caught 1/2 negatives but overlaps with item 1.

validation.gold_why: Negative sign before J is present in formula.

items.title: Nearest-neighbor sum
items.description: The energy sum is explicitly restricted to nearest-neighbor pairs along the one-dimensional chain (e.g., Σ_n s_n s_{n+1} or Σ_{<i,j>}), not over all spin pairs.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sum over wrong pairs': summing over all pairs or double-counting gives energy off by factor ~N.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a sum over all pairs Σ_{i≠j} without restricting to nearest-neighbor bonds.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Nearest-neighbor restriction defines the model; caught 0/2 but gold passed, correctness-critical.

validation.gold_why: Sum uses S_n S_{n+1} nearest-neighbor pairs.

items.title: Boltzmann distribution
items.description: The response states that the probability of a configuration {S} is proportional to exp(-E({S})/(kT)) or equivalently exp(-βE) with a negative sign in the exponent.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign in Boltzmann exponent': writing e^{+E/kT} inverts the statistical mechanics relationship.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes P ∝ e^{+E/kT}, making high-energy states more probable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Second core deliverable; caught 1/2 negatives, covers exponent sign pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Negative sign in exponent e^{-E/kT}.

items.title: Spins take values ±1
items.description: The response states or uses the convention that each spin variable at a site takes values s_i = ±1 (up or down), not {0, 1}.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong spin values': using {0,1} instead of ±1 destroys the Ising algebra; all consensus rollouts state s_i = ±1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defines spins as 0/1 or continuous variables.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Standard Ising convention; gold=FAIL and 0 discrimination, so low weight.

validation.gold_why: No mention that spins take values ±1.

items.title: J is interaction energy
items.description: The response identifies J as the interaction energy (coupling constant) between nearest-neighbor spins in the Ising model formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states 'J is the interaction energy'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the formula but never defines what J represents.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines key parameter; 0 discrimination but gold passed and needed for correctness.

validation.gold_why: J is identified as interaction energy.

items.title: k is Boltzmann's constant
items.description: The response identifies k (or k_B) as Boltzmann's constant in the Boltzmann probability formula relating probability to energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states 'k is Boltzmann's constant'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the Boltzmann formula but never defines k.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Symbol identification; 0 discrimination, low priority, reference-supported.

validation.gold_why: k identified as Boltzmann's constant.

items.title: T is temperature
items.description: The response identifies T as the temperature in the Boltzmann probability relation that connects energy to probability.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states 'T is the temperature'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the Boltzmann formula but never defines T.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Symbol identification; 0 discrimination, low priority, reference-supported.

validation.gold_why: T identified as temperature.

items.title: Lower energy, higher probability
items.description: The response explains that configurations with lower energy have higher probability in the context of statistical mechanics, as a consequence of the Boltzmann distribution.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus item: all rollouts state that lower energy means exponentially larger Boltzmann weight, which is a key explanatory deliverable of sub-question (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the formula P ∝ e^{-E/kT} but does not explain its physical meaning (lower E → higher P).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key conceptual link; caught 1/2 negatives, gold=FAIL but genuinely central to the question.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly explain lower energy gives higher probability.

items.title: Partition function normalization
items.description: The response mentions the partition function Z = Σ e^{-βE} as the normalizing constant for the probability of a configuration, or equivalently uses the proportionality symbol ∝.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing partition function': writing P = e^{-βE} as an equality without normalization gives probabilities that do not sum to 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes P({S}) = e^{-E/kT} as an equality without Z or ∝.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Proper normalization; caught 1/2 negatives, real added depth beyond bare formula.

validation.gold_why: Uses proportionality symbol ∝ for Boltzmann relation.

items.title: Beta correctly defined
items.description: If the response uses β in the Boltzmann formula, it defines β = 1/(k_B T) where k is Boltzmann's constant and T is temperature, rather than β = k_B T.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Inverted β definition': defining β = k_B T instead of 1/(k_B T) inverts the temperature dependence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defines β = kT, making higher temperature sharpen the distribution on low energy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prevents inverted-β error; 0 discrimination but correctness-critical if β is used.

validation.gold_why: β not used; condition is vacuously satisfied.

items.title: External field convention
items.description: The response states whether an external magnetic field term (-h Σ s_i) is included or deliberately omitted in the Ising energy formula for the one-dimensional model.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Unstated external field': the question does not mention a field, making the convention ambiguous if not stated.
provenance.discriminates: A response that silently includes or omits the field term without acknowledging the choice.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies scope; caught 1/2 negatives, gold=FAIL, genuine but secondary depth.

validation.gold_why: No mention of external field term.

items.title: Spins on one-dimensional chain
items.description: The response conveys that spins are arranged on a one-dimensional chain (lattice) with nearest-neighbor interactions between adjacent sites.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure specifies a one-dimensional lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions; the derivation must reflect this geometry.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a 2D or mean-field Ising formula without addressing the 1D chain structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Establishes model geometry; 0 discrimination but anchors the one-dimensional constraint.

validation.gold_why: States one-dimensional model with S_n S_{n+1}.

items.title: Derivation from pair interactions
items.description: The response explains that the total energy is obtained by summing nearest-neighbor bond energies -J s_i s_{i+1} over all adjacent pairs in the one-dimensional chain.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus item: bond energy sign convention and summation over bonds; the question asks to 'derive' not just state.
provenance.discriminates: A response that merely writes the final formula without any derivation step from individual bond energies.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Shows derivation logic; caught 1/2 negatives, gold=FAIL, real but supplementary.

validation.gold_why: No derivation explaining summation of bond energies.

items.title: Configuration notation
items.description: The response uses a configuration notation such as {S} or {s_i} to label a complete spin configuration in both the energy and probability expressions.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer uses P({S}) and E({S}) notation linking the configuration to both energy and probability.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes E and P without connecting them through a shared configuration label.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Notational clarity; 0 discrimination, minor added value for completeness.

validation.gold_why: Uses {S} notation for configuration.

items.title: Mild oligospermia diagnosis
items.description: States the most likely diagnosis is mild oligospermia.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks for the single most likely clinical diagnosis; the reference answer identifies mild oligospermia.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that diagnose normozoospermia, azoospermia, or any other condition instead of mild oligospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; the core diagnosis without which the answer is wrong.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states most likely diagnosis is mild oligospermia.

items.title: Count at lower threshold
items.description: States that the sperm count of 15 million/ml is at the lower threshold or borderline of the normal range, referencing the WHO lower reference limit of 15 million/ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on whether to apply the WHO 2010 cutoff of 15 million/ml or the older 20 million/ml cutoff; the reference frames 15 million/ml as the lower threshold.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that use an incorrect cutoff (e.g., 20 million/ml) and therefore miscalculate the degree of abnormality.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed; key reasoning anchoring why the diagnosis is mild rather than normal.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly identify WHO lower reference limit.

items.title: Motility is normal
items.description: States that the motility of 60% motile sperms is within the normal range.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Asthenozoospermia mislabel' notes that 60% motility exceeds WHO 2010 (≥40%) and older WHO (≥50%) thresholds; classifying it as abnormal is an error.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that misread 60% motility as abnormal and diagnose asthenozoospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed; supports isolating count as the sole abnormal parameter.

validation.gold_why: States motility parameters are satisfactory.

items.title: Morphology is normal
items.description: States that the morphology showing 60% normal sperms is within the normal range.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Teratozoospermia mislabel' notes that 60% normal morphology is well above all commonly used thresholds (≥4% strict; ≥30% older); classifying it as abnormal is an error.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that apply an incorrect high morphology cutoff and diagnose teratozoospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed; supports isolating count as the sole abnormal parameter.

validation.gold_why: States morphology parameters are satisfactory.

items.title: Total sperm number 30 million
items.description: Computes the total sperm number per ejaculate as 30 million by multiplying the sperm count of 15 million/ml by the volume of 2 ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts calculated the total sperm number as 30 million (15 million/ml × 2 ml).
provenance.discriminates: Responses that evaluate only concentration and never compute the total sperm number.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00 but gold=FAIL; valid intermediate calc, weighted low per gold miss.

validation.gold_why: Does not compute total sperm number of 30 million.

items.title: Below WHO 39 million limit
items.description: States that the total sperm number of 30 million is below the WHO lower reference limit of 39 million per ejaculate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Total sperm number omission' notes that 30 million is below the WHO lower limit of 39 million, making it the more definitively abnormal parameter.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that conclude the count is only borderline without recognizing the total sperm number is clearly below the WHO limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00 but gold=FAIL; key WHO threshold, weighted low per gold miss.

validation.gold_why: Does not mention total sperm number or 39 million limit.

items.title: Normal volume pH no obstruction
items.description: States that the normal volume of 2 ml and pH of 7.5 argue against obstructive causes such as CBAVD or ejaculatory duct obstruction.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus includes that volume 2 ml and pH 7.5 being normal argues against obstruction or CBAVD pattern.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not use volume and pH to rule out obstruction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; relevant differential exclusion, gold=FAIL so weighted low.

validation.gold_why: Does not discuss obstruction or volume/pH implications.

items.title: Borderline count causes infertility
items.description: States that the borderline sperm count of 15 million/ml contributes to the patient's fertility challenges despite normal findings in other semen analysis parameters.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'Despite the normal findings in other aspects of the analysis, the slightly lower sperm concentration may impact overall fertility, which aligns with a diagnosis of mild oligospermia.'
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not link the borderline count to the patient's infertility or that attribute infertility to other unproven causes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed, discrimination 0.50; ties the lab finding to the clinical presentation.

validation.gold_why: States borderline sperm concentration may impact fertility.

items.title: Other parameters all normal
items.description: States that all semen analysis parameters other than the sperm count — including pH 7.5, volume 2 ml, motility 60%, morphology 60% normal, and absence of agglutination — are normal.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree that volume, pH, motility, morphology, and agglutination status are all normal; only the sperm count is borderline.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that flag additional parameters as abnormal, leading to a combined syndrome diagnosis such as oligoasthenoteratozoospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; consolidates the non-pathologic findings, gold=FAIL so weighted low.

validation.gold_why: Only mentions motility and morphology normal; omits pH, volume, agglutination.

items.title: Fertility specialist referral
items.description: Suggests further evaluation or consultation with a fertility specialist.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer includes a suggestion to consider further evaluation or consultation with a fertility specialist, which no rollout addressed.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that provide only a diagnosis without any recommendation for further evaluation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed, discrimination 0.00; added depth, not core to the diagnosis.

validation.gold_why: Suggests consultation with a fertility specialist.

items.title: Avoids normozoospermia
items.description: Avoids diagnosing normozoospermia by treating the sperm count of 15 million/ml as fully normal without qualification.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Normozoospermia misclassification' (high severity): applying WHO 2010 ≥15 cutoff and treating exactly 15 as fully normal leads to the wrong diagnosis of normozoospermia.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that say all parameters are normal and the diagnosis is normozoospermia, missing the borderline-low count.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00, gold passed; the central trap of this question.

validation.gold_why: Does not diagnose normozoospermia; qualifies as mild oligospermia.

items.title: Avoids moderate severe label
items.description: Avoids classifying the oligospermia as moderate or severe, since the sperm count of 15 million/ml is only mildly reduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Severity overstatement': applying an older ≥20 million/ml cutoff and labelling 15 as moderate or severe oligospermia rather than mild.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that overstate severity and label the condition as moderate or severe oligospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold passed, discrimination 0.00; names a specific wrong severity, low weight.

validation.gold_why: Labels as mild only, not moderate or severe.
