items.title: GPI anchor deficiency
items.description: Identifies a deficiency of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor as the underlying molecular defect in this presentation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts diagnosed SLE and proposed defective apoptotic debris clearance; the reference identifies GPI anchor deficiency as the molecular defect.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names SLE or immune complex deposition but never mentions the GPI anchor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives with 1.00 discrimination; central molecular defect without which the answer is wrong.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly identifies GPI anchor deficiency as the molecular defect.

items.title: GPI anchor attachment role
items.description: States that the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor is necessary for the attachment of protective proteins to the cell surface.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference describes GPI anchor as necessary for attachment of various protective proteins to the cell surface.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions CD55 or CD59 without explaining that they require the GPI anchor for surface attachment.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; explains why GPI deficiency matters mechanistically but is secondary to naming the defect.

validation.gold_why: States GPI anchor necessary for attachment of protective proteins.

items.title: CD55 and CD59 lost
items.description: Names CD55 and CD59 as the specific glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored complement regulatory proteins lost from the cell surface.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly names CD55 and CD59; no rollout mentioned either protein.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses complement regulation but omits the specific surface protectins CD55 and CD59.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives with 1.00 discrimination; the two proteins are the concrete entities the question targets.

validation.gold_why: Names CD55 and CD59 as missing GPI-anchored proteins.

items.title: Complement regulation failure
items.description: States that the impaired immunological process is failure to regulate complement activity on the surface of blood cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference concludes that the impaired process is the failure to regulate complement on blood cell surfaces due to absent GPI-anchored protective proteins.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names a different impaired process such as defective apoptotic debris clearance or type III hypersensitivity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; directly answers the question's ask for the specific impaired process.

validation.gold_why: States failure to regulate complement on blood cell surfaces.

items.title: Uncontrolled complement activation
items.description: States that loss of CD55 and CD59 leads to uncontrolled complement activation on blood cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts attributed complement activation to immune complex deposition (classical pathway); the reference attributes it to loss of complement regulation by CD55 and CD59.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions complement but frames it as immune complex–triggered rather than unregulated due to missing protectins.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; key mechanistic link between protein loss and cell destruction.

validation.gold_why: States loss leads to uncontrolled complement activation on cell surfaces.

items.title: RBCs susceptible to lysis
items.description: States that absence of GPI-anchored protective proteins makes red blood cells susceptible to complement-mediated destruction.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states that lack of GPI-anchored proteins such as CD55 and CD59 on red blood cells makes them susceptible to uncontrolled complement activation and subsequent destruction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names CD55 and CD59 but does not explain that their absence renders RBCs susceptible to complement lysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; connects the molecular defect to the downstream cellular consequence.

validation.gold_why: States absence makes RBCs susceptible to complement-mediated destruction.

items.title: Intravascular hemolysis
items.description: Identifies intravascular hemolysis as the consequence of complement-mediated destruction of red blood cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states that uncontrolled complement activation causes intravascular hemolysis; no rollout identified this mechanism.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains cytopenias via bone marrow failure or immune complex nephritis rather than complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the specific type of hemolysis is critical for explaining the clinical findings.

validation.gold_why: Identifies intravascular hemolysis as consequence of complement destruction.

items.title: Hemolytic anemia correlation
items.description: States that complement-mediated destruction of red blood cells produces hemolytic anemia manifested as tea-colored urine.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly connects hemolytic anemia to the tea-colored urine presentation due to hemoglobinuria.
provenance.discriminates: A response that separates the anemia from the urinary finding or explains them through different mechanisms.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; links the mechanism to the observed anemia and urine finding.

validation.gold_why: States complement-mediated RBC destruction causes hemolytic anemia with tea-colored urine.

items.title: Hemoglobinuria from hemolysis
items.description: Attributes the tea-colored urine to hemoglobinuria resulting from intravascular hemolysis.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts interpreted tea-colored urine as glomerular hematuria from lupus nephritis; the reference explains it as hemoglobinuria from complement-mediated RBC destruction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes tea-colored urine to glomerular bleeding or nephritis rather than hemoglobinuria.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; distinguishes hemoglobinuria from hematuria, a key diagnostic point.

validation.gold_why: Attributes tea-colored urine to hemoglobinuria from intravascular hemolysis.

items.title: PNH diagnosis
items.description: Identifies the clinical diagnosis as Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts diagnosed SLE; the reference identifies PNH as the associated diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that diagnoses SLE or lupus nephritis instead of Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; diagnostic framing that contextualizes the mechanism, though the question asks for process not diagnosis.

validation.gold_why: Identifies PNH as the clinical diagnosis.

items.title: Cytopenias linked to mechanism
items.description: Links the observed anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia to the Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria and complement dysregulation mechanism.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states that the PNH process can contribute to the observed cytopenias including anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains cytopenias solely through bone marrow failure or autoimmune destruction without connecting them to the complement/GPI mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; ties the peripheral cytopenias to the underlying process rather than leaving them unexplained.

validation.gold_why: Links cytopenias to PNH and complement dysregulation mechanism.

items.title: Avoids SLE diagnosis
items.description: Avoids attributing this presentation to systemic lupus erythematosus with defective clearance of apoptotic debris and immune complexes rather than to complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts diagnosed SLE with defective apoptotic debris clearance; the reference diagnoses PNH with GPI anchor deficiency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that pattern-matches to the SLE framework using 31-year-old female plus cytopenias plus pulmonary findings.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; SLE is the primary competing diagnosis given cytopenias in a young female.

validation.gold_why: No mention of SLE; attributes presentation to complement-mediated hemolysis.

items.title: Avoids hematuria interpretation
items.description: Avoids attributing the tea-colored morning urine to glomerular hematuria or lupus nephritis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Hematuria vs hemoglobinuria' notes that all rollouts read tea-colored urine as nephritic hematuria rather than hemoglobinuria.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interprets dark urine as renal immune complex deposition rather than hemoglobinuria from intravascular hemolysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; misreading hemoglobinuria as hematuria leads to wrong workup and wrong mechanism.

validation.gold_why: Attributes urine to hemoglobinuria, not glomerular hematuria or lupus nephritis.

items.title: Avoids type III/classical pathway
items.description: Avoids naming type III hypersensitivity or classical complement pathway activation via immune complex deposition as the specific impaired immunological process.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Wrong complement mechanism' identifies type III hypersensitivity as the wrong mechanism chosen once SLE is assumed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects type III hypersensitivity and immune complex deposition instead of complement dysregulation from GPI anchor deficiency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the SLE framing naturally leads to this wrong mechanism, a shared error.

validation.gold_why: No mention of type III hypersensitivity.

items.title: GPI anchor deficiency
items.description: Identifies a deficiency of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor as the underlying molecular defect.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts diagnosed SLE and proposed defective apoptotic debris clearance; the reference identifies GPI anchor deficiency as the molecular defect.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names SLE or immune complex deposition but never mentions the GPI anchor.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly identifies GPI anchor deficiency as the molecular defect.

items.title: Two components VPL VPM
items.description: The ventral posterior nucleus of the thalamus is stated to be primarily composed of two components: the ventral posterolateral nucleus (VPL) and the ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPM).

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to identify the components; the reference answer names VPL and VPM as the two principal components.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists only one component, lists three or more, or names incorrect nuclei.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core identity of VP; caught 1/2 negatives with 0.50 discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states VP has two components: VPL and VPM.

items.title: Names VPL
items.description: The ventral posterolateral nucleus (VPL) is explicitly named as a component of the ventral posterior nucleus.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer identifies VPL as one of the two principal components.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits VPL or substitutes a different nucleus.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Essential naming; 0.00 discrimination but factually indispensable for correctness.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: The ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPM) is explicitly named as a component of the ventral posterior nucleus.

validation.gold_why: VPL is explicitly named as a component.

items.title: VPL processes body
items.description: States that the VPL processes sensory information from the body, including the arms, legs, and torso, and avoids attributing body or limb sensory input to the VPM.

items.title: GC average expression
items.description: The grand canonical thermal average of a physical quantity is written as a double sum over particle number N and microstates s, normalized by the grand partition function Ξ or equivalently by the denominator Σ_N Σ_s e^{−β(E_{N,s}−μN)}, with N appearing as a fluctuating variable in the grand canonical ensemble.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) targets the grand-canonical expectation value involving a sum over both particle number and microstates; pitfall 'Missing double sum over N' confirms this is a common failure mode.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the grand canonical average as a single sum over microstates at fixed N, effectively giving a canonical formula with a shifted energy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core derivation required by question; 0/2 discrimination but necessary for expression coverage.

validation.gold_why: No GC expression given in reference.

items.title: Ξ factorization
items.description: The grand partition function is explicitly written in the factorized form Ξ = Σ_N Z_N e^{βμN}, connecting the grand canonical ensemble to the canonical partition function Z_N across particle-number sectors.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts on the structure Ξ = Σ_N Z_N e^{βμN}; the divergent notation is cosmetic but the factorization structure is physically meaningful.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the grand canonical average without showing how Ξ decomposes into a sum over canonical partition functions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives (disc 1.00); gold=FAIL but genuinely part of the derivation linking ensembles.

validation.gold_why: No Ξ factorization in reference.

items.title: Canonical average expression
items.description: The canonical thermal average of a physical quantity is written as a single sum over microstates s at fixed particle number N, normalized by the canonical partition function Z_N = Σ_s e^{−βE_s}, with no additional sum over N in the canonical ensemble.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts on Z_N = Σ_s e^{−βE_s}; the divergent notation is cosmetic but explicit definition of Z_N is a standard part of the derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses Z_N in the average formula without ever defining it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core derivation required; 0/2 discrimination but necessary for canonical expression coverage.

validation.gold_why: No Z_N definition in reference.

items.title: Boltzmann weight signs
items.description: The grand canonical Boltzmann weight is written as e^{−β(E−μN)} with the chemical potential subtracted inside the exponent, while the canonical Boltzmann weight is e^{−βE} with no chemical potential term appearing since N is fixed in the canonical ensemble.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Sign of μN term' (high severity) identifies the mistake of writing e^{−β(E+μN)} instead of e^{−β(E−μN)}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the grand canonical weight as e^{−β(E+μN)}, which corresponds to chemical potential −μ and yields the wrong density at a given μ.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives (disc 0.50); sign of μ-term is a load-bearing formula detail.

validation.gold_why: No Boltzmann weight in reference.

items.title: Observable in numerator
items.description: The physical quantity A whose thermal average is being computed appears explicitly in the numerator of both the grand canonical and canonical average formulas, not only inside partition function definitions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Stopping at partition functions' (medium severity) identifies the mistake of writing only Ξ without displaying the full expectation value ⟨A⟩_GC.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the grand partition function Ξ but never places the observable A in the numerator of the average.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but required to show the average expression is complete rather than just defining Ξ or Z_N.

validation.gold_why: No GC numerator in reference.

items.title: Coincidence in thermodynamic limit
items.description: The response states that the grand canonical and canonical averages of a physical quantity coincide in the thermodynamic limit, considering the role of density and chemical potential.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to discuss conditions under which the two averages coincide; the reference answer states the coincidence occurs in the thermodynamic limit.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims equivalence at finite N or never states that the thermodynamic limit is required for the averages to coincide.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass; 0/2 discrimination but this is the central claim of the question.

validation.gold_why: States averages coincide in thermodynamic limit.

items.title: μ tuned to match density
items.description: The chemical potential μ is specified to be tuned so that the grand canonical mean density equals the fixed canonical density, i.e. ⟨N⟩_GC(μ, T)/V = N/V = ρ, as a condition for the averages to coincide.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Missing μ–density tuning' (high severity) identifies the mistake of claiming equivalence without requiring that μ reproduce the canonical density.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two ensembles are equivalent at the same T and μ without specifying that μ must be chosen to match the canonical density.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives (disc 0.50); matching density is the essential condition linking the two ensembles.

validation.gold_why: No mention of tuning μ to match density.

items.title: Thermodynamic limit definition
items.description: The thermodynamic limit is defined or stated as N, V → ∞ with the density ρ = N/V held fixed, as the limit in which ensemble equivalence is being discussed.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to consider the role of the thermodynamic limit; the implicit constraint specifies N, V → ∞ with N/V fixed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions the thermodynamic limit without specifying that density is held fixed as N and V diverge.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but the definition of the thermodynamic limit is necessary context for the discussion.

validation.gold_why: Thermodynamic limit not formally defined.

items.title: Fluctuations as mechanism
items.description: The response identifies the vanishing of relative particle-number fluctuations, ΔN/⟨N⟩ ~ 1/√V → 0, in the thermodynamic limit as the mechanism underlying the equivalence of the grand canonical and canonical averages.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among all three rollouts that ΔN/⟨N⟩ ~ 1/√V → 0; pitfall 'Wrong fluctuation scaling' identifies the mistake of stating 1/N instead.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states fluctuations vanish as 1/N rather than 1/√V, or that does not state the scaling at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but key reasoning connecting fluctuation scaling to ensemble equivalence.

provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly lists short-range and no-phase-transition conditions but elsewhere asserts equivalence also holds for long-range or phase-coexistence systems.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass; 0/2 discrimination but condition is in the reference answer; absorbed avoidance item 22.

validation.gold_why: Correctly limits equivalence to valid regimes.

items.title: Not near phase transitions

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Omitting pathology caveats' (medium severity, reference_contrast) identifies the mistake of claiming universal equivalence that fails for gravitational systems or first-order phase transitions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly lists short-range and no-phase-transition conditions but elsewhere asserts equivalence also holds for long-range or phase-coexistence systems.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass; 0/2 discrimination but condition is in the reference answer; absorbed avoidance item 22.

validation.gold_why: Correctly limits equivalence to valid regimes.

items.title: Pathological observables caveat
items.description: The response notes that observables sensitive to rare fluctuations may not coincide even in the thermodynamic limit, qualifying the general equivalence of grand canonical and canonical averages.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: 'The observable is a physical quantity for which thermodynamic-limit equivalence is expected; pathological observables sensitive to rare fluctuations may not coincide.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims equivalence for all observables without noting that pathological observables are excluded.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives (disc 1.00); real added depth distinguishing naive from correct ensemble equivalence.

validation.gold_why: No pathological observables caveat.

items.title: Fixed N vs fluctuating N
items.description: The response states that the canonical ensemble fixes the particle number N while the grand canonical ensemble allows N to fluctuate, as the fundamental distinction between the ensembles.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: 'The thermodynamic limit is taken as N, V → ∞ with N/V held fixed' and the structural distinction between the ensembles; the question asks to consider the role of density.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes both formulas without noting the fundamental distinction that N is fixed in one and fluctuates in the other.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but basic distinction needed for the discussion of why equivalence is nontrivial.

validation.gold_why: No fixed vs fluctuating N contrast.

items.title: Saddle-point dominance
items.description: The response explains that in the thermodynamic limit the grand canonical sum over N is dominated by the saddle-point value corresponding to the canonical particle number, justifying the equivalence.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks to discuss conditions for coincidence; the saddle-point or Laplace argument connecting the GC sum to fixed-N canonical is the standard derivation of equivalence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the fluctuation scaling without explaining how the GC sum over N collapses to the canonical fixed-N value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives (disc 0.50); provides the mathematical mechanism behind ensemble equivalence.

items.title: Same temperature condition

provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but a necessary implicit condition for the two averages to be compared at all.

items.title: Configurational integral
items.description: The configurational integral Q_N is written as ∫ d^{3N}r exp[−β Σ_{i<j} U(r_ij)] using the pairwise potential energy function.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires an expression for the canonical partition function or configurational integral with pairwise U(r_ij); consensus_correct confirms this form across all rollouts.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes Z_N without the configurational integral over pairwise interactions, or that omits the Boltzmann factor exp(−βU).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational definition; 0/3 discrimination but coverages the pairwise-interaction sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Configurational integral formula not written explicitly.

items.title: Partition function prefactor
items.description: The partition function Z_N includes the factor 1/(N!λ^{3N}) multiplied by the configurational integral, where λ is the thermal wavelength.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the partition function (not just the configurational part); consensus_correct confirms Z_N = (1/(N!λ^{3N})) Q_N.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents only Q_N = ∫ d^{3N}r e^{−βU} and calls it the partition function, omitting the kinetic prefactor and the 1/N! indistinguishability factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for the full partition function; 0/3 discrimination but no near-duplicate covers it.

validation.gold_why: Kinetic prefactor 1/(N!λ^{3N}) not mentioned.

items.title: Pairwise additivity
items.description: The total potential energy is expressed as a sum over distinct pairs: U_total = Σ_{i<j} U(r_ij).

provenance.evidence_detail: The question states 'considering the potential energy of pairwise interactions'; the implicit_constraints section confirms pairwise additivity is assumed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the total potential energy as a single many-body function rather than a sum of pairwise contributions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core assumption of the model; 0/3 discrimination but anchors the pairwise interaction structure.

validation.gold_why: Pairwise sum not explicitly written out.

items.title: Integral yields VU0
items.description: The integral of the potential energy term yields VU0, where V is the volume of the system and U0 is a constant.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts expressed the result using the Mayer f-function integral I(T)=∫[e^{−βU}−1]d³r instead of VU0; the reference explicitly states the result is VU0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents ∫[e^{−βU(r)}−1]d³r as the primary result instead of VU0, or that never states the result as V times a constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central result; 3/3 discrimination and essential to the answer's correctness.

validation.gold_why: Reference explicitly states result yields VU0.

items.title: Sequential integration steps
items.description: The step-by-step evaluation describes integrating over the position of one particle while holding the other fixed (yielding a constant) and then integrating over the second particle's position across the system volume (yielding the factor V).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states the result is 'obtained by first integrating over the position of one particle, holding the other particle fixed, and then integrating over the position of the second particle,' which produces the volume factor V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes VU0 without explaining that the V prefactor comes from the second integration over the free particle's position in the system volume.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged sources; 2/3 discrimination, directly shows the requested step-by-step derivation.

validation.gold_why: V factor origin not explicitly explained.

items.title: Physical significance
items.description: The physical significance of the VU0 result is stated as describing the behavior of a weakly interacting gas in the thermodynamic limit.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks for physical significance; the reference states it 'describes the behavior of a weakly interacting gas in the thermodynamic limit.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the physical interpretation entirely or gives only generic statements about interactions without mentioning the thermodynamic limit or weakly interacting gas behavior.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 3/3 discrimination; covers the explicit significance sub-question, gold=pass.

validation.gold_why: Physical significance stated as thermodynamic limit behavior.

items.title: Finite range invoked
items.description: The finite range of U(r) and its decay to zero at large distances are explicitly invoked to justify convergence of the potential energy integral.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Convergence condition dropped' identifies that responses treat the integral as automatically convergent without using the stated conditions; the question explicitly provides that U(r) has finite range and decays to zero.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ∫U(r)d³r without ever mentioning that the finite range or decay of U(r) guarantees convergence.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Uses the stated assumption; 0/3 discrimination and gold=FAIL, so low weight.

validation.gold_why: Finite range and decay not explicitly invoked.

items.title: U0 as spatial integral
items.description: The constant U0 is identified as the spatial integral of U(r) over relative coordinate space, U0 = ∫ U(r) d³r, and is shown to be independent of the fixed particle's position because U depends only on relative separation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference says the integral yields VU0 with U0 a constant; the agreement analysis notes all rollouts failed to state U0 = ∫U(r)d³r, instead substituting the Mayer f-function form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the result is VU0 but never defines what U0 is in terms of an integral over U(r).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged; 3/3 discrimination each, genuinely necessary for VU0 to be meaningful, gold=FAIL so capped at 4.

validation.gold_why: U0 only called a constant; integral form not given.

items.title: Weak-interaction linearization
items.description: The response explicitly applies the weak-interaction approximation to linearize the Boltzmann factor, such as e^{−βU} ≈ 1 − βU, before evaluating the integral of the potential energy term.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall on the Mayer f-function and the agreement analysis both note that the weak-interaction limit (linearizing e^{−βU}) is needed to arrive at the VU0 result rather than the full Mayer cluster integral.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the full Mayer f-function e^{−βU}−1 without applying the weak-interaction linearization that produces the direct VU0 result.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step; 1/3 discrimination, load-bearing for the derivation.

validation.gold_why: Linearization e^{-βU}≈1−βU not applied.

items.title: Ideal gas limit
items.description: The partition function reduces to the ideal gas result V^N/(N!λ^{3N}) when the potential energy U(r) is set to zero.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus_correct section confirms that all rollouts recovered the ideal gas limit Q_N^{id} = V^N when U = 0; this is a basic consistency check on the derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose partition function does not reduce to the ideal gas form when interactions are turned off.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sanity check; 0/3 discrimination and not asked for explicitly, minimal weight.

validation.gold_why: Ideal gas limit not discussed.

items.title: Thermodynamic connection
items.description: The physical significance connects the VU0 correction to a measurable thermodynamic quantity such as the second virial coefficient or the pressure deviation from the ideal gas equation of state.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks for physical significance; the question_structure target for (c) mentions 'relation to the second virial coefficient, deviation from ideal-gas behaviour, pressure correction.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that states physical significance only as 'interactions matter' without connecting VU0 to the second virial coefficient or the equation of state.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added depth; 1/3 discrimination, real but secondary significance.

validation.gold_why: No connection to virial coefficient or pressure.

items.title: Avoids Mayer f-function
items.description: Avoids presenting the Mayer f-function integral ∫[e^{−βU(r)}−1]d³r as the primary interaction result instead of VU0 obtained by direct integration of U(r).

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts substituted the Mayer cluster integral I(T)=∫[e^{−βU}−1]d³r as the main result, while the reference states the result is VU0 from direct integration of the potential energy term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that replaces the direct integral of U(r) with the Mayer f-function integral and never arrives at the VU0 form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 3/3 discrimination but pitfall advantage discounted; names the observed wrong path.

validation.gold_why: No Mayer f-function presented; VU0 is primary result.

items.title: Avoids COM coordinates
items.description: Avoids using a center-of-mass and relative coordinate transformation to evaluate the integral of the potential energy term, instead using sequential fixed-particle integration.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'COM instead of sequential integration' notes all rollouts used ∫d³R d³r rather than fixing one particle and integrating over the other, which the reference explicitly requests.
provenance.discriminates: A response that exclusively uses COM/relative coordinates and never describes holding one particle fixed while integrating over the other.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 3/3 but pitfall advantage discounted; the expected method is sequential integration.

items.title: Avoids sign error

items.title: Core energy-scale condition
items.description: States that the energy scale of the interaction between clusters is small compared to the energy differences between different internal states of the clusters.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Reversed energy inequality' (high severity).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00, gold=pass; this is the central inequality the entire derivation hinges on.

validation.gold_why: Correct direction: interaction small vs internal differences.

items.title: Off-diagonal coupling suppressed
items.description: States that off-diagonal matrix elements of the inter-cluster interaction that couple different internal states must be small compared to the internal energy differences, explicitly analyzing how interactions between clusters affect the validity of the rule.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Interaction sub-question dropped' (high severity); all rollouts addressed this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states only the parity rule and energy hierarchy without discussing inter-cluster interactions at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; the precise matrix-element statement is the load-bearing technical condition beyond the qualitative inequality.

validation.gold_why: No mention of matrix elements coupling internal states suppressed.

items.title: Nonzero interactions allowed
items.description: Avoids requiring strictly zero interaction between clusters; states that small nonzero interactions are permitted as long as their matrix elements coupling internal states are small compared to internal energy differences.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Requires zero interaction' (medium severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that sets V_12 = 0 as a necessary condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00, gold=pass; both flawed responses demanded zero interaction, a common over-restriction.

validation.gold_why: Small nonzero interactions permitted, not zero required.

items.title: Excitation gap not just binding
items.description: Avoids stating only a binding-energy condition; includes the excitation-gap condition that interaction energy must be small compared to internal excitation energy differences.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Binding energy replaces excitation gap' (medium severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses only E_b >> U_int without requiring Delta_exc >> U_int.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00, gold=pass; both flawed responses substituted binding energy for the excitation-gap criterion.

validation.gold_why: Includes excitation-gap condition; no binding-energy-only statement.

items.title: Rule is approximation
items.description: Avoids asserting that the Ehrenfest-Oppenheimer rule is exact; instead frames it as an approximation whose validity depends on stated physical conditions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Rule treated as exact' (high severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents the parity-counting rule as universally valid with no qualifying inequalities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50, gold=pass; one flawed response treated the rule as exact, a conceptual error worth flagging.

validation.gold_why: Frames rule as 'sufficient approximation' depending on conditions.

items.title: Binding and breakup energy
items.description: States that the binding energy of each cluster must exceed the inter-cluster interaction energy scale so that clusters remain bound and are not dissociated.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Breakup threshold ignored' (low severity).

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; a necessary supporting condition ensuring the composite objects persist as identifiable clusters.

validation.gold_why: No mention of breakup energy.

items.title: Spatial separation condition
items.description: States that the separation between clusters must be large compared to the internal size of the clusters so that constituent wavefunctions do not significantly overlap.

provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the spatial overlap condition entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50; wavefunction separation underpins the distinguishability of clusters as composites.

validation.gold_why: No mention of spatial separation.

items.title: Thermal energy subdominant
items.description: States that thermal energy k_B T must be small compared to the internal excitation energy differences of the clusters.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 1 and 3 include thermal energy; rollout 2 includes it within E_ext.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits thermal energy from the hierarchy of energy scales.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; thermal excitation of internal states would invalidate the statistics assignment.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: States that the relative kinetic energy between clusters must be small compared to the internal excitation energy differences of the clusters.

validation.gold_why: No mention of thermal energy.

validation.gold_why: No mention of degeneracy energy.

items.title: Timescale separation

provenance.discriminates: A response that gives no timescale or adiabaticity requirement.

validation.gold_why: No mention of timescale separation.

validation.gold_why: No mention of point-like treatment.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.50, gold=pass; one flawed response gave only vague qualitative claims without quantitative comparison.

validation.gold_why: Uses 'small compared to' expressing an inequality of energy scales.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states 'Malformations in these structures can lead to facial deformities like mandibular hypoplasia and ear anomalies, which align with the symptoms observed.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the arches but does not connect their malformations to the specific facial deformities of mandibular hypoplasia and malformed ears.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; links arch malformations to observed clinical findings.

validation.gold_why: States arch malformations cause mandibular hypoplasia and ear anomalies.

items.title: Deafness from ear malformation
items.description: States that congenital deafness results from malformation of external or middle ear structures derived from pharyngeal arches.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts attributed deafness to external and middle ear maldevelopment from pharyngeal arch defects.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes deafness to inner ear or central nervous system causes rather than pharyngeal arch-derived ear structures.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL but clinically necessary; explains deafness through arch derivatives.

validation.gold_why: Does not explicitly link deafness to ear structure malformation.

items.title: Airway compromise link
items.description: Links mandibular hypoplasia to airway compromise that necessitates tracheostomy placement and mechanical ventilation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts connected micrognathia from mandibular hypoplasia to airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes mandibular hypoplasia without connecting it to the airway compromise and tracheostomy findings.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL but clinically necessary; explains respiratory findings through mandible.

validation.gold_why: Does not link mandibular hypoplasia to airway compromise or tracheostomy.

items.title: Avoids neural crest as structure
items.description: Avoids naming cranial neural crest cells as the embryonic structure instead of the first and second pharyngeal arches.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Neural crest vs arches' pitfall (high severity): all rollouts named cranial neural crest cells as THE answer, but the reference concludes the first and second pharyngeal arches are the embryonic structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents cranial neural crest cells as the final answer for the embryonic structure rather than naming the pharyngeal arches.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; prevents misidentifying neural crest as the answer.

validation.gold_why: Names pharyngeal arches, not neural crest cells, as the structure.

items.title: Avoids naming only first arch
items.description: Avoids naming only the first pharyngeal arch without including the second pharyngeal arch.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Omitting second arch' pitfall (high severity): naming only the first arch ignores second arch contributions to external ear, stapes, and hyoid.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies the first pharyngeal arch alone as the responsible structure, omitting the second pharyngeal arch.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; prevents incomplete answer naming only first arch.

validation.gold_why: Names both first and second pharyngeal arches.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Maxwell's equations setup
items.description: Writes Maxwell's equations for the medium with dielectric constant ε = ε0 + δε (curl H = (ε/c)∂E/∂t, curl E = -(1/c)∂H/∂t), and states that the incident wave E0, H0 satisfies Maxwell's equations with the uniform dielectric constant ε0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires starting from Maxwell's equations in the inhomogeneous medium; the reference opens with the full system.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps directly to a wave equation without showing the starting Maxwell's equations for ε = ε0 + δε.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but necessary foundational setup for the derivation.

validation.gold_why: Maxwell's equations with ε explicitly written.

items.title: Field decomposition
items.description: Decomposes the total fields as E = E0 + E' and H = H0 + H', identifying E0, H0 as the incident waves and E', H' as the scattered waves.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes E = E_0 + E', H = H_0 + H' as the key step enabling linearization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts a perturbation expansion without explicitly writing the incident-plus-scattered field decomposition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but required step enabling the linearization.

validation.gold_why: Fields decomposed as E=E0+E', H=H0+H'.

items.title: Linearization
items.description: States that products of the small quantities E', H', and δε (such as δε·E' or δε·H') are neglected in the approximation linear in δε.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree this linearization step is load-bearing; responses that retain δε·E' produce a self-consistent rather than first-Born source.
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps δε·E' terms, producing a nonlinear (Born-iterated) equation instead of the linearized one.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; core approximation that enables the entire reduction.

validation.gold_why: Products of small quantities E', H', δε neglected.

items.title: Polarization source
items.description: Identifies the polarization source as δP = (E0/(4π))δε in Gaussian units (or a unit-consistent SI equivalent), proportional to the incident field E0 and the deviation δε.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'wrong field in source' pitfall: responses may write δP ∝ δε·E (total field) or δε·E' (scattered field) instead of δε·E_0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes δP proportional to the total field E or the scattered field E' instead of the incident field E_0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; defines the key source term for scattered radiation.

validation.gold_why: δP = E0 δε/(4π) explicitly given.

items.title: Linearized Maxwell system
items.description: Writes the linearized Maxwell equations for the scattered fields: curl H' - (ε0/c)∂E'/∂t = (4π/c)∂(δP)/∂t, curl E' + (1/c)∂H'/∂t = 0, div(ε0 E') = -4π div(δP), and div H' = 0 (or SI-equivalent).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly writes this equation as the central result of the linearization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that moves the source to the left-hand side with a wrong sign, or omits the source term entirely from the curl equation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but the derived system is the central result of the problem.

validation.gold_why: Sourced curl equation for scattered fields written.

items.title: Dipole interpretation
items.description: Interprets each volume element dV of the medium as a vibrating dipole with dipole moment δP dV = (E0 δε/(4π)) dV (or SI-equivalent), constituting the source of scattered light.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question explicitly asks to show the source is 'additional sources in the form of vibrating dipoles, distributed in the medium'; the reference states δP dV is the dipole moment.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the source term mathematically but never identifies it as a distribution of vibrating dipoles with moment δP dV.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1/2 discrimination; directly addresses the dipole-source requirement.

validation.gold_why: Each dV is dipole with moment δP dV.

items.title: Uniform medium conclusion
items.description: Concludes that the medium can be regarded as uniform with dielectric constant ε0, in which the non-uniformities are equivalent to additional distributed dipole sources that produce the scattered radiation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) explicitly asks to show the problem reduces to propagation in a uniform medium with additional dipole sources; the reference states this conclusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives the linearized equations but never states the physical conclusion that the medium is effectively uniform ε0 with dipole sources.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination but states the problem's central conclusion.

validation.gold_why: Concludes uniform medium ε0 with dipole sources.

items.title: Superposition argument
items.description: States that superposition of scattered fields E' = Σ E'_i follows from the linearity and homogeneity of the linearized Maxwell system with respect to both (E', H') and δε, connecting the decomposition δε = Σ δ_i ε to an additive decomposition of the source δP.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states 'linearity and homogeneity of system (4) with respect both to the fields E', H' and to δε'; rollouts cited only 'linearity of the wave operator' which is less precise.
provenance.discriminates: A response that justifies superposition only by invoking 'linearity of the wave operator' without stating the system is linear and homogeneous in both the fields and δε simultaneously.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 and 1/2 discrimination; highest-signal item, addresses second sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Superposition from linearity and homogeneity stated.

items.title: Scattered intensity small
items.description: States that the intensity of the scattered field is small compared with that of the incident wave, providing the physical justification for the linear approximation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states 'the intensity of the scattered field is small compared with that of the incident wave' before substituting and neglecting products.
provenance.discriminates: A response that performs the linearization algebra without stating the physical reason (small scattered intensity) that justifies dropping products of small quantities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; high-signal justification for linearization.

validation.gold_why: Scattered intensity small compared to incident.

items.title: Bound charge identification
items.description: Identifies the bound charge density associated with the dipole distribution as −div(δP), arising from the divergence equation div(ε0 E') = −4π div(δP).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes div(ε0 E') = -4π div(δP), which directly shows the bound charge; no rollout exhibited this connection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the divergence equation but does not interpret -div(δP) as an effective bound charge density.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; provides physical depth beyond the core derivation.

validation.gold_why: div(δP) appears as bound charge source term.

items.title: Cross-terms second-order
items.description: Avoids retaining cross-terms such as δ_i ε · E'_j (with i≠j) in the superposition argument, recognizing they are second-order in δε and therefore neglected.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'multiple scattering retained' pitfall: responses may insert the decomposition δε = Σ δ_i ε into the full nonlinear expression without re-linearizing, leaving spurious cross-coupling terms.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims superposition holds without addressing why cross-terms between different non-uniformities vanish, or that retains multiple-scattering coupling terms.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 2/2 discrimination; observed pitfall where flawed responses kept cross-terms.

validation.gold_why: Cross-products δ_iε·E'_j not explicitly discussed.

items.title: Unit convention consistency
items.description: Avoids mixing unit conventions by ensuring the 1/(4π) factor in δP appears only when Maxwell's equations are written in Gaussian form, and not when using SI conventions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on units: rollouts 1–2 used Gaussian (δP = δε E_0/(4π)), rollout 3 used SI (P_eff = ε_0 δε E_0); the pitfall is internal inconsistency, not the choice itself.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes curl H = (ε/c)∂E/∂t (Gaussian) but then δP = δε·E_0 without the 1/(4π) factor, or vice versa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0/2 discrimination; real but untested pitfall, given minimal weight.

validation.gold_why: Gaussian units used consistently throughout.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Blue precipitate is Fe²⁺
items.description: States the blue precipitate with potassium ferricyanide is due to the presence of ferrous (Fe²⁺) ions, not ferric (Fe³⁺) ions.

items.title: Names craniopharyngioma
items.description: The response names craniopharyngioma as the specific mass lesion directly causing this 11-year-old boy's symptoms of vomiting, morning headaches, and visual field narrowing.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 1 and 2 diagnosed posterior fossa masses (medulloblastoma/ependymoma) while the reference specifies craniopharyngioma; this is the central divergent point.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that diagnose a posterior fossa tumor or give only a generic 'brain tumor' without naming craniopharyngioma.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination across all three sources; the central diagnosis.

validation.gold_why: Names craniopharyngioma explicitly.

items.title: Suprasellar location
items.description: The response specifies that the craniopharyngioma is located in the suprasellar region.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference names 'suprasellar region' as the lesion location, distinguishing it from posterior fossa localization given by incorrect rollouts.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that localize the mass to the posterior fossa, fourth ventricle, or brainstem.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; localizes the lesion precisely as required.

validation.gold_why: States suprasellar region.

items.title: Optic chiasm compression
items.description: The response attributes the narrowing of visual fields to direct mass-effect compression of the optic chiasm by the suprasellar mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 1 and 2 attributed visual field narrowing to papilledema; the reference states craniopharyngiomas compress the optic chiasm, leading to progressive narrowing of visual fields.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that attribute visual field narrowing to papilledema rather than direct chiasmal compression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination from both sources; explains the visual symptoms.

validation.gold_why: Attributes visual field narrowing to optic chiasm compression.

items.title: Pediatric age group
items.description: The response notes that craniopharyngiomas are common in this age group, consistent with the 11-year-old boy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states 'Craniopharyngiomas are common in this age group'; rollouts did not provide this epidemiological justification.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that give a diagnosis without supporting pediatric epidemiology.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; supports why this lesion is most likely.

validation.gold_why: Notes craniopharyngiomas common in this age group.

items.title: Unifying single lesion
items.description: The response explains both the increased intracranial pressure-related symptoms and the visual field narrowing as caused by a single suprasellar mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Separating symptom clusters' pitfall warns against treating visual field narrowing and raised-ICP symptoms as independent problems; the reference unifies them under one craniopharyngioma.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that propose separate mechanisms for vomiting/headaches versus visual field narrowing.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination from source 7; avoids split diagnoses.

validation.gold_why: Single suprasellar mass explains both symptom sets.

items.title: Increased ICP mechanism
items.description: The response identifies increased intracranial pressure as the mechanism behind the vomiting and occasional headaches.

provenance.evidence_detail: This is the required direct causal mechanism for the pressure-related symptoms; all three rollouts and the reference agree on raised ICP.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that attribute vomiting and headaches to a non-pressure mechanism such as primary gastrointestinal disease.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.00 discrimination but covers sub-question on mechanism; necessary for completeness.

validation.gold_why: Identifies increased ICP as mechanism.

items.title: Progressive field loss
items.description: The response describes progressive narrowing of visual fields as a feature of optic chiasm compression by the craniopharyngioma.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference specifies 'progressive narrowing of visual fields' as the pattern produced by chiasmal compression.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that present the visual field defect as acute or non-progressive.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; adds specificity about the visual deficit pattern.

validation.gold_why: Describes progressive narrowing of visual fields.

items.title: Morning symptom pattern
items.description: The response links the morning worsening of symptoms to increased intracranial pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: Morning worsening is a classic raised-ICP pattern that the reference ties to the craniopharyngioma causing CSF obstruction.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that fail to connect morning symptom worsening to raised intracranial pressure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.00 discrimination; adds clinical reasoning depth on symptom timing.

validation.gold_why: Links morning worsening to increased ICP.

items.title: CSF flow obstruction
items.description: The response states that obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow produces the increased intracranial pressure symptoms.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference specifies 'obstructing cerebrospinal fluid flow, resulting in increased intracranial pressure-related symptoms'; rollouts specified particular obstruction sites instead.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that state raised ICP arises without identifying CSF flow obstruction as the mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 0.00 discrimination; identifies the pathophysiological link from mass to ICP.

validation.gold_why: States CSF flow obstruction causes increased ICP.

items.title: CN II sparing distinction
items.description: The response explains that a suprasellar craniopharyngioma can compress the optic chiasm while sparing cranial nerves III through XII.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Ignoring localizing clue' pitfall identifies that intact cranial nerves point away from posterior fossa/brainstem lesions toward a suprasellar location.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that ignore the intact cranial nerve exam or use a posterior fossa lesion despite preserved cranial nerves.
provenance.calibration_rationale: High discrimination (3/3) but gold=FAIL; adds real clinical depth on intact cranial nerves.

validation.gold_why: Does not explain intact CNs supporting suprasellar lesion.

items.title: Avoids posterior fossa
items.description: Avoids diagnosing a posterior fossa tumor such as medulloblastoma as the direct cause of this 11-year-old boy's symptoms.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Posterior fossa default' pitfall, observed in rollouts 1 and 2, selects medulloblastoma without accounting for the visual field narrowing.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that name medulloblastoma, ependymoma, or another posterior fossa mass as the lesion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; common pediatric pitfall in lesion localization.

validation.gold_why: No posterior fossa tumor mentioned.

items.title: Avoids papilledema cause
items.description: Avoids attributing the mild narrowing of visual fields to papilledema from increased intracranial pressure rather than optic chiasm compression.

provenance.discriminates: Responses that explain visual field narrowing solely as papilledema secondary to raised ICP.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Perfect 1.00 discrimination; distinguishes chiasm compression from ICP-related visual loss.

validation.gold_why: Visual fields attributed to chiasm compression, not papilledema.

items.title: Circulatory changes mechanism

items.title: RVT causes hematuria

items.title: Landau gauge stated
items.description: The response states the landau gauge vector potential explicitly, choosing A = (0, Bx, 0) or A = (-By, 0, 0) with the magnetic field applied along the z-direction, and avoids switching the gauge convention mid-derivation.

items.title: Hamiltonian with confinement
items.description: The response writes the single-particle Hamiltonian in the landau gauge including a confining potential, of the form H = p_x²/(2m) + (p_y + eBx)²/(2m) + V(x).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) demands a detailed derivation of edge-state wavefunctions including the effect of confinement, which requires this Hamiltonian.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes only the bulk Landau Hamiltonian without adding V(x).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step; disc=0 but the Hamiltonian is the load-bearing scaffold for all downstream results.

validation.gold_why: Reference never writes the Hamiltonian.

items.title: B sign fixed along z
items.description: The response fixes the sign of the magnetic field along the z-direction (e.g. B > 0 along +z) and keeps it consistent throughout the derivation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'B-field sign unset' (severity medium) flags failing to commit to a sign for B.
provenance.discriminates: A response that leaves B as an unsigned magnitude and thus cannot assign chirality direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sign consistency is necessary for current direction; disc=0 due to limited negatives but genuinely correctness-bearing.

validation.gold_why: Reference never fixes B sign.

items.title: Guiding center sign
items.description: The response gives the guiding-center coordinate as x_0 = -k_y ℓ_B² = -ℏk_y/(eB) for electron charge q = -e with the landau gauge vector potential A = (0, Bx, 0) and magnetic field applied along the z-direction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign of guiding center' (severity high) flags writing x_0 = +k_y ℓ_B².
provenance.discriminates: A response with the wrong sign of x_0, which reverses the chirality at every edge.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sign of x_0 determines chirality; disc=0.50 (caught 1/2 negatives), high importance to final result.

validation.gold_why: Reference never gives guiding-center coordinate.

items.title: Bulk wavefunctions derived
items.description: The response derives the quantum Hall bulk wavefunctions ψ_{n,k}(x,y) = (1/√L_y) e^{ik_y y} φ_n(x - x_0), defines the magnetic length ℓ_B = √(ℏ/(eB)), and shows φ_n are harmonic oscillator functions of width ℓ_B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks for a detailed derivation of the wavefunctions; all correct rollouts produce this form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the energy levels but never writes the explicit spatial wavefunctions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core deliverable of the derivation; disc=0 but correctness collapses without proper wavefunctions.

validation.gold_why: Reference never derives bulk wavefunctions.

items.title: Bulk Landau level energies
items.description: The response gives the bulk landau level energies E_n = ℏω_c(n + 1/2) with cyclotron frequency ω_c = eB/m and notes they are flat (degenerate) in k_y before the confining potential is applied.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) requires the eigenvalues; the flatness is the starting point for edge dispersion and chirality.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives edge dispersion without first establishing the flat bulk levels.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate result establishing the degeneracy that the edge then lifts; disc=0.

validation.gold_why: Reference never gives Landau level energies.

items.title: Edge-dispersed energy
items.description: The response shows the confining potential near the edge of the sample lifts the landau-level degeneracy in k_y, giving E_n(k_y) ≈ ℏω_c(n + 1/2) + V(x_0), and avoids stopping the derivation at the flat bulk levels.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question_structure implicit constraints note that confinement breaks translation invariance near the edges and lifts degeneracy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the edge dispersion as arising from the magnetic field alone rather than from the confining potential.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Edge dispersion is the mechanism behind chirality; absorbed two avoidance items and translation-breaking criterion.

validation.gold_why: Reference never states confinement breaks translation.

items.title: Group velocity along y
items.description: The response derives the group velocity along the y-direction as ⟨v_y⟩ = (1/ℏ)∂E/∂k_y = -V'(x_0)/(eB), using the minimal-coupling velocity v_y = (p_y + eBx)/m rather than the bare momentum p_y/m.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Dropped vector-potential term in j_y' (severity high).
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ⟨j_y⟩ = ℏk_y/m, a constant with no edge dependence or chirality.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate linking dispersion to current; absorbed the bare-momentum pitfall.

validation.gold_why: Reference does not use bare momentum as current.

items.title: Electrical current j_y
items.description: The response gives the electrical current along the y-direction as ⟨j_y⟩ = q⟨v_y⟩ = -e·[-V'(x_0)/(eB)] = +V'(x_0)/B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks for the expectation value of the current; the pitfall 'Current vs velocity' shows the charge factor is load-bearing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports ⟨v_y⟩ as the current without multiplying by q = -e.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Primary requested quantity; disc=0.50 (caught 1/2 negatives), sign directly determines chirality.

validation.gold_why: Reference never gives electrical current.

items.title: Bulk current vanishes
items.description: The response notes that in the bulk where V'(x_0) = 0 the current ⟨j_y⟩ vanishes, so only the edge of the sample carries current.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts explicitly contrast the zero bulk current with the nonzero edge current; omitting this leaves chirality unmotivated.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies current flows everywhere rather than being localized near the edge.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Highest discrimination: disc=1.00 (caught 2/2 negatives); distinguishes edge-only transport from bulk conduction.

validation.gold_why: Reference never notes bulk current vanishes.

items.title: B reversal reverses chirality
items.description: The response states that reversing the magnetic field along the z-direction reverses all edge current directions, as a signature of chirality.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'B-field sign unset' (severity medium) notes the chirality direction must be tied to the sign of B.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fixes B but never connects the sign of B to the propagation direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc=0.50 (caught 1/2 negatives); reinforces chirality concept with B-dependence.

validation.gold_why: Reference never addresses B reversal.

items.title: Completing the square shift
items.description: The response includes the completing-the-square step for a linearized confining potential, giving the shifted center x_c = x_0 - V'(x_0)/(mω_c²) and the energy correction -[V'(x_0)]²/(2mω_c²).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 1 and 3 included this higher-order correction while rollout 2 stopped at leading order; it is genuine extra depth.
provenance.discriminates: A response with only the leading-order dispersion E_n + V(x_0) and no wavefunction offset.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Disc=1.00 (caught 2/2 negatives); advanced detail adding depth beyond the standard derivation.

validation.gold_why: Reference never includes completing-the-square step.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question gives 'insists on further investigations and treatment despite reassurances' as a key feature, and the reference cites disproportionate thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to symptoms.

validation.gold_why: Mentions insistence on further tests despite reassurances.

items.title: Symptoms genuinely experienced
items.description: The response indicates that the symptoms are genuinely experienced rather than intentionally produced or feigned, reflecting genuine concern about health without evidence of underlying medical pathology.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts included the point that symptoms are not intentionally feigned, and the reference frames genuine concern about health.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies the patient is fabricating symptoms for secondary gain.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; distinguishes SSD from factitious or malingering.

validation.gold_why: States genuine concern without evidence of pathology.

items.title: Links features to criteria
items.description: The response links the clinical features of normal physical examinations, persistent somatic symptoms, and insistence on further investigations to the diagnostic criteria for somatic symptom disorder.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states the clinical features align with somatic symptom disorder and briefly justifies the diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the diagnosis with no connection to the case details.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; synthesizes case features into diagnostic reasoning.

validation.gold_why: Links clinical features to SSD diagnostic criteria.

items.title: Avoids illness anxiety misdiagnosis
items.description: Avoids diagnosing illness anxiety disorder, which requires minimal or absent somatic symptoms rather than prominent nausea, vomiting, and leg pain.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Illness Anxiety vs SSD' flags the temptation to select illness anxiety due to the insistence on testing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects illness anxiety disorder as the final diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; the closest differential trap with real clinical risk.

validation.gold_why: Does not diagnose illness anxiety disorder.

items.title: Avoids no-diagnosis conclusion
items.description: Avoids concluding that no psychiatric diagnosis applies because physical examination and lab investigations are normal.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stopping at normal workup' warns that normal findings can delay psychiatric diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that recommends continued reassurance only and offers no diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Zero discrimination but common real-world trap; normal labs do not exclude SSD.

validation.gold_why: Does give a psychiatric diagnosis despite normal labs.

items.title: Differentiates from illness anxiety
items.description: The response distinguishes somatic symptom disorder from illness anxiety disorder by noting that the patient has prominent somatic symptoms rather than minimal symptoms with fear of illness.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure flags differentiation from illness anxiety disorder as an implicit constraint; the reference and all correct rollouts favor SSD due to prominent somatic symptoms.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects illness anxiety disorder because of the help-seeking behavior.

validation.gold_why: No distinction from illness anxiety disorder is made.

items.description: The response connects the exonuclease proofreading activity to determining the base substitution mutation rate in human chromosomes.

items.title: Volume to mL
items.description: The response converts 1.00 gal of octane to 3785 mL before applying the density 0.7025 g/mL.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary setup step; caught 0/3 negatives because flawed responses also converted units correctly.

items.title: Moles of octane
items.description: The response calculates 23.28 mol of C8H18 using a molar mass of 114.2 g/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference and all rollouts agree on 23.28 mol as the amount of octane.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong molar mass or makes an arithmetic error, yielding a different mole value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary intermediate; caught 0/3 negatives but correct mole count is essential for final scaling.

validation.gold_why: Calculates 23.28 mol using 114.2 g/mol.

items.title: Target reaction equation
items.description: The response writes the target incomplete-combustion reaction as C8H18 + 17/2 O2 → 8CO + 9H2O with correct stoichiometric coefficients.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states C8H18 + 17/2 O2 → 8CO + 9H2O; rollouts did not write this equation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the complete combustion equation (8CO2) or balances with 19/2 O2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/3 negatives; correct stoichiometry for incomplete combustion is a key discriminator.

validation.gold_why: Writes C8H18 + 17/2 O2 → 8CO + 9H2O.

items.title: Back-calculated ΔHf result
items.description: The response back-calculates ΔH_f°(C8H18) = -64.6 kcal/mol from the given ΔH_comb of -1302.7 kcal/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference derives ΔH_f°(C8H18) = -64.6 kcal; no rollout performed this back-calculation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts the target reaction enthalpy without first deriving ΔH_f°(C8H18).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; this load-bearing intermediate result is essential for the target reaction enthalpy.

validation.gold_why: Back-calculates ΔH_f°(C8H18) = -64.6 kcal/mol.

items.title: Rearranged expression
items.description: The response rearranges the combustion enthalpy equation to solve for ΔH_f°(C8H18) as +1302.7 + 8(−94.05) + 9(−68.32) kcal/mol or an algebraically equivalent form.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference shows ΔH_f°(C8H18) = +1302.7 + 8(-94.05) + 9(-68.32) = -64.6 kcal; rollouts never wrote this rearrangement.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states ΔH_f°(C8H18) = -64.6 kcal without showing the rearrangement, or uses the wrong signs when rearranging.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the rearranged algebra verifies the method, not just the numerical result.

validation.gold_why: Shows rearranged expression matching criterion.

items.title: Avoids direct ΔH_comb use
items.description: Avoids using the supplied ΔH_comb = -1302.7 kcal/mol directly as the molar enthalpy for the reaction producing carbon monoxide and water vapor.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used -1302.7 kcal/mol directly for the CO-forming reaction, yielding -3.03 × 10^4 kcal instead of -15520 kcal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that multiplies 23.28 mol × (-1302.7 kcal/mol) to get approximately -3.03 × 10^4 kcal.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; this is the question's central trap—applying complete-combustion ΔH to CO products.

validation.gold_why: Uses ΔH_comb only for back-calculation, not directly.

items.title: Complete combustion equation
items.description: The response identifies the complete combustion reaction used for back-calculation as C8H18 + 25/2 O2 → 8CO2 + 9H2O.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes C8H18 + 25/2 O2 → 8CO2 + 9H2O as the reaction defining ΔH_comb; rollouts did not identify this reaction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong combustion equation or omits the O2 stoichiometry when back-calculating.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the complete-combustion equation anchors the back-calculation of ΔHf(C8H18).

validation.gold_why: Writes C8H18 + 25/2 O2 → 8CO2 + 9H2O.

items.title: Formation enthalpies in back-calc
items.description: The response uses ΔH_f°(CO2) = -94.05 kcal/mol and ΔH_f°(H2O) = -68.32 kcal/mol in the back-calculation of ΔH_f°(C8H18).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference plugs in 8 × (-94.05) and 9 × (-68.32) to solve for ΔH_f°(C8H18); rollouts did not invoke these values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses different formation enthalpy values or skips this step entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; correct standard enthalpy values prevent propagated arithmetic errors.

validation.gold_why: Uses -94.05 and -68.32 in back-calculation.

items.title: CO formation enthalpy
items.description: The response uses ΔH_f°(CO) = -26.41 kcal/mol when computing the reaction enthalpy for the formation of 8CO.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses 8 × (-26.41) in the target reaction enthalpy expression; rollouts never invoked this value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the CO2 formation enthalpy (-94.05) instead of the CO value, or omits this term.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the correct CO formation enthalpy is essential for the target reaction calculation.

validation.gold_why: Uses -26.41 kcal/mol for CO.

items.title: Water vapor enthalpy
items.description: The response uses ΔH_f°(H2O(g)) = -57.79 kcal/mol for water vapor rather than the liquid value -68.32 kcal/mol when computing the target reaction enthalpy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses 9 × (-57.79) for the H2O(g) product in the target reaction; rollouts did not reach this step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that carries the liquid water enthalpy -68.32 into the target reaction instead of using -57.79 for vapor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; distinguishing water vapor from liquid enthalpy is critical to this question.

validation.gold_why: Uses -57.79 kcal/mol for water vapor.

items.title: Molar reaction enthalpy
items.description: The response reports the molar enthalpy of the target reaction C8H18 → 8CO + 9H2O as -666.8 kcal/mol.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference computes ΔH = [8(-26.41) + 9(-57.79) - (-64.6)] = -666.8 kcal/mol; no rollout obtained this value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports -1302.7 kcal/mol, -732 kcal/mol, or any other value instead of -666.8 kcal/mol.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the per-mol enthalpy is the key intermediate result before scaling.

validation.gold_why: Reports -666.8 kcal per mol of C8H18.

items.title: Scales to sample size
items.description: The response multiplies the molar enthalpy of -666.8 kcal/mol by 23.28 mol of C8H18 to obtain the total heat produced.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference performs (-666.8 kcal/mol) × 23.28 mol = -15520 kcal as the final scaling step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the correct molar enthalpy but fails to multiply by the 23.28 mol sample size.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; scaling by moles connects the molar result to the asked quantity.

validation.gold_why: Multiplies -666.8 kcal/mol by 23.28 mol.

items.title: Final answer value
items.description: The response reports the total heat produced as -15520 kcal.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference gives ΔH = -15520 kcal as the final answer; all rollouts reported approximately -3.03 × 10^4 kcal instead.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports -3.03 × 10^4 kcal (from using -1302.7 directly) or any other value instead of -15520 kcal.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the final numeric answer with correct sign and magnitude.

validation.gold_why: Reports total heat as -15520 kcal.

items.title: Hess's law expression
items.description: The response applies Hess's law to the target reaction using the expression ΔH = 8·ΔH_f°(CO) + 9·ΔH_f°(H2O) − ΔH_f°(C8H18).

provenance.discriminates: A response that states -666.8 kcal/mol without showing the Hess's law expression with the correct stoichiometric coefficients.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the Hess's law expression with correct coefficients ties the calculation together.

validation.gold_why: Uses ΔH = 8ΔH_f°(CO) + 9ΔH_f°(H2O) − ΔH_f°(C8H18).
