items.title: No simultaneous frame
items.description: States that it is not possible to perform a Lorentz transformation into a frame where the two measurements are made simultaneously.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) demands a yes/no decision; the reference answer states it is not possible due to time-like separation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents only a conditional framework ('possible iff spacelike') without committing to the definitive 'no' for this scenario.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; this is the core definitive answer the question demands.

validation.gold_why: Explicitly states no Lorentz frame makes them simultaneous.

items.title: Time-like separation
items.description: States that the two measurement events are time-like separated.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on whether to identify the scenario as timelike; rollout 2 correctly did so, matching the reference, while rollout 1 left it as a conditional.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats both spacelike and timelike cases as equally plausible without recognizing the scenario is timelike.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; the physical reason why no simultaneous Lorentz frame exists.

validation.gold_why: Mentions time-like separation of measurement events.

items.title: Timelike worldline
items.description: States that a massive particle's worldline is time-like, so any two events on it satisfy c²Δt² > |Δr|², making the measurements time-like separated by construction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Worldline not treated as timelike' (severity medium): rollouts failed to recognize the scenario pins down timelike separation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the two measurement events as potentially spacelike separated, as if they were arbitrary spacetime points rather than events on a single particle's worldline.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 1.00; provides physical justification despite gold=FAIL; key reasoning step.

validation.gold_why: No mention of massive particle worldline.

items.title: Temporal ordering preserved
items.description: States that for time-like separated events, the temporal ordering is preserved across all inertial frames and no subluminal boost can make Δt' = 0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts: 'If s² > 0, no finite subluminal boost can make Δt'=0.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims a boost exists for timelike events, or that does not connect timelike separation to preservation of temporal order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.33; reinforces the core timelike argument with frame-preservation reasoning.

validation.gold_why: No statement about temporal ordering preservation.

items.title: Spacelike simultaneity condition
items.description: States as a general principle that a Lorentz boost can make two events simultaneous only if they are spacelike separated (|Δr| > c|Δt|), before applying it to the time-like scenario.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts: 'Simultaneity possible iff spacelike separated.' This general framework contextualizes the specific timelike conclusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to the timelike conclusion without establishing the general condition under which simultaneity is achievable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.33; general principle needed before applying to the time-like scenario.

validation.gold_why: No general spacelike condition stated.

items.title: Invariant interval sign
items.description: States that for time-like separation the invariant interval satisfies s² = c²Δt² − |Δr|² > 0 and avoids reversing this inequality.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts identified this condition; the sign of s² distinguishes whether simultaneity is achievable.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong sign convention or fails to connect the interval sign to the impossibility of simultaneity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.33; absorbs reversed-inequality pitfall; load-bearing mathematical criterion.

validation.gold_why: No invariant interval expression stated.

items.title: Lorentz time transform
items.description: Writes the Lorentz transformation of the time interval as Δt' = γ(Δt − v·Δr/c²).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requests mathematical derivations; consensus among all rollouts identified this formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses Lorentz transformation qualitatively without providing the quantitative time-interval transformation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.00; gold=FAIL but question explicitly requests mathematical derivations.

validation.gold_why: No Lorentz time transform formula given.

items.title: Simultaneity velocity condition
items.description: Derives the simultaneity condition v = c²Δt/|Δr| and states that it requires |v| < c for a valid Lorentz transformation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts identified this condition; checking v < c is the critical subluminal constraint.
provenance.discriminates: A response that solves for v but does not check the physical constraint that the boost must be subluminal.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.33; derives the key condition showing no valid boost exists.

validation.gold_why: No simultaneity velocity condition derived.

items.title: HUP not violated
items.description: States explicitly that the Heisenberg uncertainty principle is not violated, and addresses directly whether it would be in this scenario.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'HUP sub-question left unanswered' (severity medium): rollout 3 was truncated and never reached the HUP analysis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives the Lorentz transformation condition but never addresses sub-question (b) on whether HUP would be violated.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Discrimination 0.33; directly addresses the 'would this violate HUP' sub-question.

validation.gold_why: HUP question left unanswered in reference.

items.title: HUP relation stated
items.description: States the Heisenberg uncertainty principle as Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2, derived from the canonical commutator [x,p] = iħ.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requests derivations of the uncertainty relation; consensus among rollouts identified ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses HUP qualitatively without stating the quantitative inequality or its commutator origin.
